title.raw: 卷十九 志第九 樂一 Volume 19 Treatises 9: Music 1

sentences.zh: 志第九 樂一

translations.literal: Treatise Nine: Music One
translations.idiomatic: Treatise Nine: Music, Part One

sentences.zh: 《易》曰：「先王作樂崇德，殷薦之上帝，以配祖考。

translations.literal: The Book of Changes says: "The former kings made music to exalt virtue, and with full reverence presented offerings to the Supreme Lord, to be paired with the founding ancestors."
translations.idiomatic: The Book of Changes says: "The former kings created music to glorify virtue and, with solemn reverence, offered it to Heaven, pairing it with offerings to their royal ancestors."

sentences.zh: 」自黃帝至于三代，名稱不同。

translations.literal: From the Yellow Emperor down to the Three Dynasties, the names were not the same.
translations.idiomatic: From the Yellow Emperor through the Three Dynasties, the names of the music differed.

sentences.zh: 周衰凋缺，又為鄭衛所亂。

translations.literal: When Zhou declined, it withered and was deficient, and was further thrown into disorder by the music of Zheng and Wei.
translations.idiomatic: As Zhou declined, its music decayed and was further corrupted by the licentious tunes of Zheng and Wei.

sentences.zh: 魏文侯雖好古，然猶昏睡於古樂。

translations.literal: Marquis Wen of Wei, though he loved antiquity, still dozed through the ancient music.
translations.idiomatic: Though Marquis Wen of Wei professed a love of antiquity, he still nodded off to the ancient music.

sentences.zh: 於是滛聲熾而雅音廢矣。

translations.literal: Thereupon licentious sounds flourished while refined music was abandoned.
translations.idiomatic: Licentious music flourished, and the refined classical repertoire was cast aside.

sentences.zh: 及秦焚典籍，《樂經》用亡。

translations.literal: When Qin burned the classics, the Classic of Music thereby perished.
translations.idiomatic: When Qin burned the classics, the Classic of Music was lost as well.

sentences.zh: 漢興，樂家有制氏，但能記其鏗鏘鼓舞，而不能言其義。

translations.literal: When Han arose, among the masters of music was the Zhi clan, who could only record the clashing and drumming and the dance movements, but could not explain their meaning.
translations.idiomatic: After Han rose, the Zhi family of music masters could remember only the clangor, drums, and dance steps—they could not explain what the music meant.

sentences.zh: 周存六代之樂，至秦唯餘《韶》《武》而已。

translations.literal: Zhou preserved the music of the six dynasties; by Qin only the Shao and Wu remained.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou had preserved the music of all six previous dynasties; by Qin only the Shao and Wu dances survived.

sentences.zh: 始皇改周舞曰《五行》，漢高祖改《韶舞》曰《文始》，以示不相襲也。

translations.literal: The First Emperor changed the Zhou dance to the Wu Xing, and Emperor Gaozu of Han changed the Shao dance to the Wen Shi, to show that one did not inherit from the other.
translations.idiomatic: The First Emperor renamed the Zhou dance Wu Xing; Gaozu renamed the Shao dance Wen Shi—each change signaling that the new dynasty would not simply inherit the old ritual names.

sentences.zh: 又造《武德舞》，舞人悉執干戚，以象天下樂已行武以除亂也。

translations.literal: He also created the Wu De dance; the dancers all held shields and axes, to symbolize that all under Heaven rejoiced that military force had been exercised to remove disorder.
translations.idiomatic: He also created the Wu De dance, in which every dancer bore shield and battle-axe to signify that the realm rejoiced once war had cleared away chaos.

sentences.zh: 故高祖廟奏《武德》《文始》《五行》之舞。

translations.literal: Therefore at Gaozu's temple were performed the dances Wu De, Wen Shi, and Wu Xing.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu's ancestral temple therefore featured the Wu De, Wen Shi, and Wu Xing dances.

sentences.zh: 周又有《房中之樂》，秦改曰《壽人》。

translations.literal: Zhou also had the Music of the Inner Chamber; Qin changed its name to Longevity Man.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou also had the Music of the Inner Chamber, which Qin renamed Longevity Man.

sentences.zh: 其聲，楚聲也，漢高好之；

translations.literal: Its sound was Chu music, which Gaozu of Han loved;
translations.idiomatic: Its melody was in the Chu style, which Gaozu favored;

sentences.zh: 孝惠改曰《安世》。

translations.literal: Emperor Hui changed its name to An Shi (Peace Through Ages).
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Hui renamed it An Shi (Peace Through Ages).

sentences.zh: 高祖又作《昭容樂》、《禮容樂》。

translations.literal: Gaozu also composed the Zhao Rong music and the Li Rong music.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu also composed the Zhao Rong and Li Rong pieces.

sentences.zh: 《昭容》生於《武德》，《禮容》生於《文始》《五行》也。

translations.literal: Zhao Rong derived from Wu De; Li Rong derived from Wen Shi and Wu Xing.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Rong grew out of Wu De; Li Rong grew out of Wen Shi and Wu Xing.

sentences.zh: 漢初，又有《嘉至樂》，叔孫通因秦樂人制宗廟迎神之樂也。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Han there was also the Jia Zhi music; Shusun Tong, relying on Qin musicians, devised the music for welcoming the spirits in the ancestral temple.
translations.idiomatic: Early Han also had the Jia Zhi piece; Shusun Tong, working with Qin musicians, composed the temple music for welcoming the spirits.

sentences.zh: 文帝又自造《四時舞》，以明天下之安和。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen also personally created the Four Seasons dance, to show that all under Heaven was at peace and harmony.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen personally created the Four Seasons dance to proclaim peace and harmony throughout the realm.

sentences.zh: 盖樂先王之樂者，明有法也；

translations.literal: To perform the music of the former kings was to show that there was a precedent to follow;
translations.idiomatic: Performing the music of former kings showed that one honored established precedent;

sentences.zh: 樂己所自作者，明有制也。

translations.literal: to perform music of one's own creation was to show that there was regulation.
translations.idiomatic: performing music of one's own creation showed that the dynasty had its own ritual order.

sentences.zh: 孝景采《武德舞》作《昭德舞》，薦之太宗之廟。

translations.literal: Emperor Jing adapted the Wu De dance into the Zhao De dance and presented it at the temple of the Great Ancestor.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Jing adapted the Wu De dance into the Zhao De dance and offered it at the temple of the Great Ancestor.

sentences.zh: 孝宣采《昭德舞》為《盛德舞》，薦之世宗之廟。

translations.literal: Emperor Xuan adapted the Zhao De dance into the Sheng De dance and presented it at the temple of the World Ancestor.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xuan adapted the Zhao De dance into the Sheng De dance and offered it at the temple of the World Ancestor.

sentences.zh: 漢諸帝奏《文始》《四時》《五行》之舞焉。

translations.literal: The various emperors of Han performed the dances Wen Shi, Four Seasons, and Wu Xing.
translations.idiomatic: Han emperors in general performed the Wen Shi, Four Seasons, and Wu Xing dances.

sentences.zh: 武帝時，河間獻王與毛生等共采《周官》及諸子言樂事者，以著《樂記》，獻八佾之舞，與制氏不相殊。

translations.literal: In the time of Emperor Wu, the King of Hejian and Mao Sheng and others together gathered passages on music from the Offices of Zhou and from the various masters, to compile the Record of Music, and presented the eight-row dance, which differed in no way from that of the Zhi clan.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Wu, the King of Hejian, Mao Sheng, and others collected material on music from the Offices of Zhou and various masters to compile the Record of Music; they also presented the eight-row dance, which was essentially the same as what the Zhi family had preserved.

sentences.zh: 其內史中丞王定傳之，以授常山王禹。

translations.literal: The Palace Secretary and Censor-in-Chief Wang Ding transmitted it and handed it on to Yu, King of Changshan.
translations.idiomatic: Palace Secretary and Censor-in-Chief Wang Ding passed it down to Yu, King of Changshan.

sentences.zh: 禹，成帝時為謁者，數言其義，獻記二十四卷。

translations.literal: Yu, who under Emperor Cheng served as Usher, often expounded its meaning and presented the record in twenty-four scrolls.
translations.idiomatic: Yu served as court usher under Emperor Cheng, lectured repeatedly on its meaning, and submitted the twenty-four-scroll Record.

sentences.zh: 劉向校書，得二十三篇，然竟不用也。

translations.literal: Liu Xiang collated the books and obtained twenty-three chapters, yet in the end it was not adopted.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Xiang collated the text and recovered twenty-three chapters, but the court never put them into use.

sentences.zh: 至明帝初，東平憲王蒼總定公卿之議，曰：「宗廟宜各奏樂，不應相襲，所以明功德也。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Emperor Ming's reign, the Filial and Worthy King of Dongping, Cang, summarized the deliberations of the high ministers and said: "Each ancestral temple ought to have its own music performed; they should not inherit one another's pieces, for this is how merit and virtue are made clear."
translations.idiomatic: Early in Emperor Ming's reign, the Filial and Worthy King of Dongping, Cang, summarized the ministers' debate: "Each ancestral temple should have its own music; pieces should not simply be inherited from one reign to the next, for that is how merit and virtue are distinguished."

sentences.zh: 承《文始》《五行》《武德》為《大武之舞》。

translations.literal: Taking over Wen Shi, Wu Xing, and Wu De, he made the Great Wu dance.
translations.idiomatic: He combined Wen Shi, Wu Xing, and Wu De into the Great Wu dance.

sentences.zh: 」又制舞歌一章，薦之光武之廟。

translations.literal: " He also composed one chapter of dance-song and presented it at the temple of Emperor Guangwu.
translations.idiomatic: " He also composed a dance-song and offered it at Guangwu's temple.

sentences.zh: 漢末大亂，眾樂淪缺。

translations.literal: At the end of Han came great disorder, and the various musics were lost and deficient.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of Han, civil war left the court repertoire in ruins.

sentences.zh: 魏武平荊州，獲杜夔，善八音，常為漢雅樂郎，尤悉樂事，於是以為軍謀祭酒，使剏定雅樂。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wu of Wei pacified Jing province he obtained Du Kui, skilled in the eight kinds of sound, who had long served as Han's officer of refined music and knew music affairs especially well; he was therefore made Libationer for Military Planning and charged with creating and fixing the refined music.
translations.idiomatic: When Cao Cao pacified Jing province he captured Du Kui, a master of the eight-tone ensemble who had served Han as a refined-music officer and knew ritual music inside out. Cao made him Libationer for Military Planning and put him in charge of restoring court music.

sentences.zh: 時又有鄧靜、尹商，善訓雅樂，歌師尹胡能歌宗廟郊祀之曲，舞師馮肅、服養曉知先代諸舞，夔悉總領之。

translations.literal: At that time there were also Deng Jing and Yin Shang, skilled in teaching refined music; the song-master Yin Hu could sing the pieces for the ancestral temple and suburban sacrifices; the dance-masters Feng Su and Fu Yang understood the various dances of former ages—Kui took charge of them all.
translations.idiomatic: Deng Jing and Yin Shang were adept at teaching court music; song-master Yin Hu knew the temple and suburban sacrifice hymns; dance-masters Feng Su and Fu Yang knew the dances of earlier dynasties. Du Kui oversaw them all.

sentences.zh: 遠考經籍，近采故事，魏復先代古樂，自夔始也。

translations.literal: Examining the classics at a distance and gathering recent precedents, Wei restored the ancient music of former ages—this began with Kui.
translations.idiomatic: Drawing on the classics and recent precedent alike, Wei restored the ancient court repertoire—work that began with Du Kui.

sentences.zh: 而左延年等，妙善鄭聲，惟夔好古存正焉。

translations.literal: Yet Zuo Yannian and others were wonderfully skilled in the music of Zheng; only Kui loved antiquity and preserved what was correct.
translations.idiomatic: Zuo Yannian and others excelled at the popular music of Zheng; only Du Kui clung to antiquity and kept the court tradition upright.

sentences.zh: 文帝黃初二年，改漢《巴渝舞》曰《昭武舞》，改宗廟《安世樂》曰《正世樂》，《嘉至樂》曰《迎靈樂》，《武德樂》曰《武頌樂》，《昭容樂》曰《昭業樂》，《雲翹舞》曰《鳳翔舞》，《育命舞》曰《靈應舞》，《武德舞》曰《武頌舞》，《文始舞》曰《大韶舞》，《五行舞》曰《大武舞》。

translations.literal: In the second year of Huangchu under Emperor Wen, the Han Ba-Yu dance was changed to the Zhao Wu dance; in the ancestral temple, An Shi music became Zheng Shi music, Jia Zhi music became Ying Ling music, Wu De music became Wu Song music, Zhao Rong music became Zhao Ye music, Yun Qiao dance became Feng Xiang dance, Yu Ming dance became Ling Ying dance, Wu De dance became Wu Song dance, Wen Shi dance became Great Shao dance, and Wu Xing dance became Great Wu dance.
translations.idiomatic: In Huangchu year 2, Emperor Wen renamed Han pieces for the new dynasty: the Ba-Yu dance became Zhao Wu; temple music An Shi became Zheng Shi, Jia Zhi became Ying Ling, Wu De became Wu Song, Zhao Rong became Zhao Ye; Yun Qiao became Feng Xiang, Yu Ming became Ling Ying; the Wu De dance became Wu Song, Wen Shi became Great Shao, and Wu Xing became Great Wu.

sentences.zh: 其眾歌詩，多即前代之舊；

translations.literal: Of the many songs and poems, most were simply those of the previous dynasty;
translations.idiomatic: Most of the hymns and lyrics were still those of Han;

sentences.zh: 唯魏國初建，使王粲改作《登歌》及《安世》、《巴渝》詩而已。

translations.literal: only when Wei was first established did they have Wang Can revise the Ascent Hymn and the poems for An Shi and Ba-Yu.
translations.idiomatic: only at Wei's founding did Wang Can revise the Ascent Hymn and the An Shi and Ba-Yu lyrics.

sentences.zh: 明帝太和初，詔曰；

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Taihe era under Emperor Ming, an edict said:
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Taihe era, Emperor Ming issued an edict:

sentences.zh: 「禮樂之作，所以類物表庸而不忘其本者也。

translations.literal: "Ritual and music are made in order to classify things, display merit, and not forget their root.
translations.idiomatic: "Ritual and music exist to classify things, display merit, and keep their origins in view.

sentences.zh: 凡音樂以舞為主，自黃帝《雲門》以下，至於周《大武》，皆太廟舞名也。

translations.literal: In general music takes dance as its chief element; from the Yellow Emperor's Cloud Gate down to Zhou's Great Wu, all are names of dances for the Grand Temple.
translations.idiomatic: Music is fundamentally dance-led: from the Yellow Emperor's Cloud Gate through Zhou's Great Wu, these are all names of ancestral-temple dances.

sentences.zh: 然則其所司之官，皆曰太樂，所以總領諸物，不可以一物名。

translations.literal: Accordingly the office that oversees them is all called Grand Music, because it has general charge of the various elements and cannot be named after a single thing.
translations.idiomatic: The office that oversees them should therefore be called Grand Music, since it governs every element of the rite and cannot be named after a single dance.

sentences.zh: 武皇帝廟樂未稱，其議定廟樂及舞，舞者所執，綴兆之制，聲歌之詩，務令詳備。

translations.literal: The temple music of Emperor Wu has not yet been properly titled; deliberate on fixing the temple music and dances, what the dancers hold, the pattern of positions and markers, and the poems for the vocal music—see that all are fully provided.
translations.idiomatic: The temple music for Emperor Wu still lacks proper titles. Deliberate on the temple music and dances, the dancers' regalia, stage markings, and hymn texts, and make the whole system complete.

sentences.zh: 樂官自如故為太樂。

translations.literal: The music officers shall as before be called Grand Music."
translations.idiomatic: Restore the music officers' former title of Grand Music."

sentences.zh: 」太樂，漢舊名，後漢依讖改大予樂官，至是改復舊。

translations.literal: Grand Music was the old Han name; Later Han, following a prophecy, changed it to Grand Bestower of Music; now it was changed back to the former usage.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Music was Han's old title; Later Han, following a prophecy, had renamed the office Grand Bestower of Music; now the original name was restored.

sentences.zh: 於是公卿奏曰：「臣聞德盛而化隆者，則樂舞足以象其形容，音聲足以發其歌詠。

translations.literal: Thereupon the high ministers memorialized: "Your subjects have heard that when virtue is abundant and transformation is far-reaching, then dance is sufficient to image one's form and bearing, and sound is sufficient to give voice to one's songs of praise.
translations.idiomatic: The high ministers then submitted: "We have heard that when virtue is great and transformation far-reaching, dance can embody a ruler's bearing and music can voice his praise.

sentences.zh: 故薦之郊廟，而鬼神享其和；

translations.literal: Therefore when offered in the suburban altars and temples, the spirits enjoy its harmony;
translations.idiomatic: Offered at suburban altars and temples, it wins the spirits' harmonious acceptance;

sentences.zh: 用之朝廷，則君臣樂其度。

translations.literal: when used at court, ruler and ministers rejoice in its measure.
translations.idiomatic: used at court, ruler and ministers delight in its measure.

sentences.zh: 使四海之內，徧知至德之盛，而光煇日新者，禮樂之謂也。

translations.literal: To cause all within the four seas broadly to know the fullness of supreme virtue, and that its radiance renews day by day—this is what is meant by ritual and music.
translations.idiomatic: To spread supreme virtue throughout the realm so that its radiance renews daily—that is the purpose of ritual and music.

sentences.zh: 故先王殷薦上帝，以配祖考，盖當其時而制之矣。

translations.literal: Therefore the former kings with full reverence offered to the Supreme Lord and paired him with the founding ancestors—assuredly they fashioned these things in their own time.
translations.idiomatic: The former kings offered to Heaven with full reverence and paired Heaven with the royal ancestors; they fashioned ritual music for their own age.

sentences.zh: 周之末世，上去唐、虞幾二千年，《韶》《箾》《南》《籥》《武》《象》之樂，風聲遺烈，皆可得而論也。

translations.literal: At the end of Zhou, going back to Tang and Yu was nearly two thousand years, yet the music of Shao, Xiao, Nan, Yue, Wu, and Xiang—the lingering renown of their style—could all still be discussed.
translations.idiomatic: Even at Zhou's end, nearly two thousand years after Tang and Yu, the reputations of Shao, Xiao, Nan, Yue, Wu, and Xiang could still be discussed.

sentences.zh: 由斯言之，禮樂之事，弗可以已。

translations.literal: From this it is said that the affairs of ritual and music cannot be set aside.
translations.idiomatic: From this we see that ritual and music must never be abandoned.

sentences.zh: 今太祖武皇帝樂宜曰《武始之樂》。

translations.literal: Now the music of the Grand Ancestor, Emperor Wu, ought to be called the Music of Martial Beginning.
translations.idiomatic: The music of the Grand Ancestor, Emperor Wu, should be titled Music of Martial Beginning.

sentences.zh: 武，神武也；

translations.literal: Wu means divine martial prowess;
translations.idiomatic: Wu means divine martial prowess;

sentences.zh: 武，又跡也。

translations.literal: wu also means footprint.
translations.idiomatic: wu also means footprint.

sentences.zh: 言神武之始，又王跡所起也。

translations.literal: It speaks of the beginning of divine martial power and also of where the royal footprint arose.
translations.idiomatic: The title marks both the dawn of divine martial power and the place where the royal enterprise began.

sentences.zh: 高祖文皇帝樂宜曰《咸熙之舞》。

translations.literal: The music of the High Ancestor, Emperor Wen, ought to be called the Dance of Universal Flourishing.
translations.idiomatic: The music of the High Ancestor, Emperor Wen, should be titled the Dance of Universal Flourishing.

sentences.zh: 咸，皆也，熙，興也，言應受命之運，天下由之皆興也。

translations.literal: Xian means all; xi means to flourish—speaking of responding to the mandate of fate, so that all under Heaven through it all flourished.
translations.idiomatic: Xian means "all"; xi means "flourish"—signifying that Heaven's mandate was answered and the whole realm rose with it.

sentences.zh: 至於羣臣述德論功，建定烈祖之稱，而未制樂舞，非所以昭德紀功。

translations.literal: As for the ministers recounting virtue and discussing merit, establishing the title of Illustrious Ancestor, yet not devising music and dance—this is not how to display virtue and record achievement.
translations.idiomatic: The ministers have praised merit and established the title Illustrious Ancestor, yet no music or dance has been composed—virtue and achievement cannot be displayed that way.

sentences.zh: 夫歌以詠德，舞以象事。

translations.literal: Song is to chant virtue; dance is to image events.
translations.idiomatic: Song praises virtue; dance embodies deeds.

sentences.zh: 於文，文武為斌，兼秉文武，聖德所以章明也。

translations.literal: In writing, wen and wu combine into bin; holding both wen and wu together is how sagely virtue is made manifest.
translations.idiomatic: In the written form, wen and wu combine into bin (patterned brilliance); holding civil and martial excellence together is how sagely virtue is displayed.

sentences.zh: 臣等謹制樂舞名《章斌之舞》。

translations.literal: Your subjects respectfully devise a music-and-dance called the Dance of Manifest Pattern.
translations.idiomatic: We respectfully propose a music-and-dance titled the Dance of Manifest Pattern.

sentences.zh: 昔《簫韶》九奏，親於虞帝之庭，《武》《象》《大武》，亦振於文、武之阼。

translations.literal: Formerly the Xiao Shao was performed nine times in person in the court of the Lord of Yu; Wu, Xiang, and Great Wu likewise resounded on the eastern steps of Wen and Wu.
translations.idiomatic: In antiquity the Xiao Shao was performed nine times in Yu's court; Wu, Xiang, and Great Wu resounded on the eastern steps of Kings Wen and Wu.

sentences.zh: 特以顯其德教，著其成功，天下被服其光煇，習詠其風聲者也。

translations.literal: It was solely to display their virtue and teaching, make clear their achievements, cause all under Heaven to submit to their radiance, and accustom them to chant their renown.
translations.idiomatic: They displayed virtue and teaching, recorded achievement, and let the realm submit to their radiance and learn their fame in song.

sentences.zh: 自漢高祖、文帝各逮其時，而為《武德》《四時》之舞，上考前代制作之宜，以當今成業之美，播揚弘烈，莫盛於《章斌》焉。

translations.literal: Since Gaozu and Emperor Wen of Han each reached their own time and made the Wu De and Four Seasons dances, looking up to examine what was fitting in the productions of former ages and taking the beauty of today's completed enterprise, to spread and exalt the great achievement—none is greater than Zhang Bin.
translations.idiomatic: Han Gaozu and Emperor Wen each composed dances for their own age—the Wu De and Four Seasons dances. Surveying earlier models and today's achievements, no dance could spread the dynasty's glory more fully than Zhang Bin.

sentences.zh: 《樂志》曰：『鐘磬干戚，所以祭先王之廟，又所以獻酬酳酢也。

translations.literal: The Treatise on Music says: "Bells, chimes, shields, and axes are used to sacrifice in the temples of the former kings, and also to present offerings in the exchange of toasts at the feast."
translations.idiomatic: The Treatise on Music says: "Bells, stone chimes, shields, and axes serve sacrifice in the temples of former kings and also the exchange of toasts at the feast."

sentences.zh: 在宗廟之中，君臣莫不致敬；

translations.literal: Within the ancestral temple, ruler and ministers none fail to show reverence;
translations.idiomatic: Within the ancestral temple, ruler and ministers all pay reverence;

sentences.zh: 族長之中，長幼無不從和。

translations.literal: among the clan elders, old and young none fail to follow in harmony.
translations.idiomatic: among the clan elders, young and old all join in harmony.

sentences.zh: 』故仲尼答賓牟賈之問曰：『周道四達，禮樂交通。

translations.literal: " Therefore Confucius, answering Binmou Jia's question, said: "The Way of Zhou extends in all four directions; ritual and music interpenetrate.
translations.idiomatic: " Confucius answered Binmou Jia: "The Way of Zhou reaches in every direction; ritual and music interweave."

sentences.zh: 』《傳》云：『魯有禘樂，賓祭用之。

translations.literal: " The Commentary says: "Lu had Di music, used at the guest sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: The Commentary says: "Lu had Di music, used at the guest sacrifice."

sentences.zh: 』此皆祭禮大享，通用盛樂之明文也。

translations.literal: " All these are clear texts that at the great offerings of sacrificial ritual, splendid music is used in common.
translations.idiomatic: These are explicit statements that grand sacrificial feasts employ full ceremonial music.

sentences.zh: 今有事於天地宗廟，則此三舞宜並以為薦享；

translations.literal: Now when there are rites for Heaven and Earth and the ancestral temples, these three dances ought all to be used together as offerings;
translations.idiomatic: When rites are performed for Heaven, Earth, and the ancestral temples, these three dances should all be offered together;

sentences.zh: 及臨朝大享，亦宜舞之。

translations.literal: and at the court's great feast they should also be danced.
translations.idiomatic: and they should be danced at the court's great feast as well.

sentences.zh: 然後乃合古制事神訓民之道，關於萬世，其義益明。

translations.literal: Only then will it accord with the ancient system of serving the spirits and instructing the people—a matter bearing on ten thousand generations, and its meaning will be the clearer.
translations.idiomatic: Only then will practice accord with the ancient way of serving the spirits and instructing the people—a matter for ten thousand generations, and its meaning will stand clear.

sentences.zh: 又臣等思惟，三舞宜有總名，可名《大鈞之樂》。

translations.literal: Moreover your subjects have reflected that the three dances ought to have a collective name; they may be called the Music of the Great Balance.
translations.idiomatic: We further propose a collective name for the three dances: the Music of the Great Balance.

sentences.zh: 鈞，平也。

translations.literal: Jun means balance.
translations.idiomatic: Jun means balance.

sentences.zh: 言大魏三世同功，以至隆平也。

translations.literal: It speaks of the three generations of Great Wei sharing in achievement, reaching abundant peace.
translations.idiomatic: It signifies that three generations of Wei shared in founding the dynasty and brought the realm to abundant peace.

sentences.zh: 於名為美，於義為當。

translations.literal: As a name it is beautiful; in meaning it is fitting.
translations.idiomatic: The name is elegant and the meaning apt.

translations.literal: " The Masters of Writing memorialized: "It should be as submitted above.
translations.idiomatic: " The Masters of Writing reported: "The proposal should be adopted as submitted."

translations.literal: " At first the emperor did not permit the creation of the Zhang Bin music;
translations.idiomatic: " At first the emperor refused to authorize the Zhang Bin music;

sentences.zh: 三請，乃許之。

translations.literal: after three requests he then granted it.
translations.idiomatic: after three petitions he consented.

sentences.zh: 於是尚書又奏：「祀圓丘以下，《武始舞》者，平冕，黑介幘，玄衣裳，白領袖，絳領袖中衣，絳合幅袴，絳𥿉，黑韋鞮。

translations.literal: Thereupon the Masters of Writing again memorialized: "For sacrifices from the Round Mound downward, for the Martial Beginning dance: plain cap, black kerchief, dark upper and lower garments, white collar and sleeves, crimson collar and sleeves on the inner robe, crimson joined-panel trousers, crimson gaiters, black leather shoes.
translations.idiomatic: The Masters of Writing then reported the dancers' dress: for rites from the Round Mound altar downward, performers of the Martial Beginning dance wear a plain cap, black kerchief, dark robes with white collar and sleeves, crimson-trimmed inner garment, crimson trousers, crimson gaiters, and black leather shoes.

sentences.zh: 《咸熙舞》者，冠委貎，其餘服如前。

translations.literal: For the Universal Flourishing dance: the cap of Wei Mao; the rest of the dress as before.
translations.idiomatic: For the Universal Flourishing dance: the Wei Mao cap; the rest as above.

sentences.zh: 《章斌舞》者，與《武始》《咸熙》舞者同服。

translations.literal: For the Manifest Pattern dance: the same dress as the dancers of Martial Beginning and Universal Flourishing.
translations.idiomatic: For the Manifest Pattern dance: the same costume as the Martial Beginning and Universal Flourishing dancers.

sentences.zh: 奏於朝庭，則《武始舞》者，武冠，赤介幘，生絳袍單衣，絳領袖，皂領袖中衣，虎文畫合幅袴，白布𥿉，黑韋鞮。

translations.literal: When performed at court, for the Martial Beginning dance: martial cap, red kerchief, unbleached crimson robe as single garment, crimson collar and sleeves, black collar and sleeves on the inner robe, tiger-pattern painted joined-panel trousers, white cloth gaiters, black leather shoes.
translations.idiomatic: At court performance, Martial Beginning dancers wear a martial cap, red kerchief, unbleached crimson robe, crimson collar and sleeves, black-trimmed inner garment, tiger-pattern trousers, white gaiters, and black leather shoes.

sentences.zh: 《咸熙舞》者，進賢冠，黑介幘，生黃袍單衣，白合幅袴，其餘服如前。

translations.literal: For the Universal Flourishing dance: the cap of advancing worth, black kerchief, unbleached yellow robe as single garment, white joined-panel trousers; the rest of the dress as before.
translations.idiomatic: Universal Flourishing dancers wear the cap of advancing worth, black kerchief, unbleached yellow robe, white trousers, and the remaining items as above.

sentences.zh: 」奏可。

translations.literal: " The memorial was approved.
translations.idiomatic: " The memorial was approved.

sentences.zh: 史臣案：《武始》《咸熙》二舞，冠制不同，而云《章斌》與《武始》《咸熙》同服，不知服何冠也？

translations.literal: The historiographer comments: The two dances Martial Beginning and Universal Flourishing have different cap regulations, yet it says Manifest Pattern shares dress with Martial Beginning and Universal Flourishing—one does not know which cap it wears.
translations.idiomatic: The historiographer notes: Martial Beginning and Universal Flourishing require different caps, yet the text says Manifest Pattern shares their dress—so which cap did those dancers wear?

sentences.zh: 侍中繆襲又奏：「《安世歌》本漢時歌名。

translations.literal: Attendant-in-Ordinary Miao Xi again memorialized: "The An Shi song was originally a Han-era song title.
translations.idiomatic: Attendant-in-Ordinary Miao Xi submitted again: "An Shi was originally a Han song title.

sentences.zh: 今詩歌非往詩之文，則宜變改。

translations.literal: Now if the poem and song are not the text of the former poem, then the title ought to be changed.
translations.idiomatic: If the present lyrics are no longer the old text, the title should be changed.

sentences.zh: 案《周禮》注云：《安世樂》，猶周《房中之樂》也。

translations.literal: According to the commentary on the Rites of Zhou: An Shi music is like Zhou's Music of the Inner Chamber.
translations.idiomatic: The commentary on the Rites of Zhou says that An Shi music corresponds to Zhou's Music of the Inner Chamber.

sentences.zh: 是以往昔議者，以《房中》歌後妃之德，所以風天下，正夫婦，宜改《安世》之名曰《正始之樂》。

translations.literal: Therefore former debaters, taking the Inner Chamber as singing the virtue of the empress and consorts, thereby to instruct all under Heaven and rectify husband and wife, held that the name An Shi ought to be changed to the Music of Correct Beginning.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier debaters held that the Inner Chamber praised the empress's virtue to instruct the realm and regulate marriage, and therefore proposed renaming An Shi as Music of Correct Beginning.

sentences.zh: 自魏國初建，故侍中王粲所作《登歌》《安世詩》，專以思詠神靈及說神靈鑒享之意。

translations.literal: Since Wei was first established, the late Attendant-in-Ordinary Wang Can composed the Ascent Hymn and the An Shi poem, devoted solely to contemplating and chanting the spirits and explaining that the spirits observe and enjoy the offerings.
translations.idiomatic: Since Wei's founding, the late Wang Can composed the Ascent Hymn and An Shi lyrics devoted solely to praising the spirits and declaring that they witness and accept the offerings.

sentences.zh: 襲後又依歌省讀漢《安世歌》詠，亦說『高張四縣，神來燕享，嘉薦令儀，永受厥福』。

translations.literal: Xi later, following the song, carefully read the Han An Shi song's chant; it too says, "High are hung the four sets of bells; the spirits come to feast in ease; fine offerings and excellent rites—may they forever receive this blessing."
translations.idiomatic: Xi later reviewed the Han An Shi lyrics line by line; they too say, "High hang the four bell-sets; the spirits come to feast at ease; fine offerings and excellent rites—may they forever receive this blessing."

sentences.zh: 無有《二南》后妃風化天下之言。

translations.literal: There is nothing of the Two Souths' language about the empress transforming all under Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: They contain nothing of the Two Souths' praise of the empress civilizing the realm.

sentences.zh: 今思惟往者謂《房中》為后妃之歌者，恐失其意。

translations.literal: Now on reflection, those who formerly called the Inner Chamber a song of the empress and consorts perhaps missed its meaning.
translations.idiomatic: On reflection, those who treated the Inner Chamber as a hymn to the empress may have misunderstood its purpose.

sentences.zh: 方祭祀娛神，登堂歌先祖功德，下堂歌詠燕享，無事歌后妃之化也。

translations.literal: At the time of sacrifice one delights the spirits; ascending the hall one sings the achievements of the founding ancestors; descending the hall one chants the feast—there is no occasion to sing of the empress's transforming influence.
translations.idiomatic: Sacrifice is meant to delight the spirits: on the upper hall one sings the ancestors' merit; on the lower hall one chants the feast—there is no place for hymns to the empress's civilizing influence.

sentences.zh: 自宜依其事以名其樂歌，改《安世歌》曰《享神歌》。

translations.literal: It is fitting to name the music-song according to its matter; change the An Shi song to the Song for Enjoying the Spirits.
translations.idiomatic: The piece should be named for its function; rename the An Shi song the Song for Enjoying the Spirits.

sentences.zh: 」奏可。

translations.literal: " The memorial was approved.
translations.idiomatic: " The memorial was approved.

sentences.zh: 案：文帝已改《安世》為《正始》，而襲至是又改《安世》為《享神》，未詳其義。

translations.literal: Note: Wen Di had already changed An Shi to Zheng Shi, yet Xi by this time again changed An Shi to Xiang Shen—the meaning is not clear.
translations.idiomatic: It should be noted that Wen Di had already renamed An Shi as Zheng Shi, yet Xi at this point again renamed An Shi as Xiang Shen; the rationale is unclear.

sentences.zh: 王粲所造《安世詩》，今亡。

translations.literal: The An Shi poem that Wang Can composed is lost today.
translations.idiomatic: The An Shi poem composed by Wang Can is no longer extant.

sentences.zh: 襲又奏曰：「文昭皇后廟，置四縣之樂，當銘顯其鈞奏次第，依太祖廟之名號，曰昭廟之具樂。

translations.literal: Xi again memorialized, saying, "At Empress Wen Zhao's temple, since four bell-sets of music are installed, the order of the graduated performance should be inscribed and displayed; following the naming pattern of the Founding Emperor's temple, call it 'The Complete Music of the Zhao Temple.'
translations.idiomatic: Xi memorialized again: "At Empress Wen Zhao's temple, where four bell-sets are installed, the sequence of the graduated performance should be inscribed and made clear. Following the naming convention of the Founding Emperor's temple, it should be called 'The Complete Music of the Zhao Temple.'

sentences.zh: 」尚書奏曰：「禮，婦人繼夫之爵，同牢配食者，樂不異文。

translations.literal: " The Ministerial Court memorialized, saying, "In ritual, when a woman succeeds her husband's rank and shares the paired sacrifice, the music does not differ in form.
translations.idiomatic: " The Ministerial Court replied: "By ritual, when a woman inherits her husband's rank and shares the paired sacrifice, the music does not differ in form.

sentences.zh: 昭皇后今雖別廟，至於宮縣樂器音，均宜如襲議。

translations.literal: Though Empress Zhao now has a separate temple, as for the suspended bell instruments and tones, all should accord with Xi's proposal.
translations.idiomatic: Although Empress Zhao now has her own temple, the suspended bells, instruments, and tones should all follow Xi's proposal.

sentences.zh: 」奏可。

translations.literal: " The memorial was approved.
translations.idiomatic: " The memorial was approved.

sentences.zh: 散騎常侍王肅議曰：「王者各以其禮制事天地，今說者據《周官》單文為經國大體，懼其局而不知弘也。

translations.literal: Wang Su, Attendant Cavalier at Large, argued, saying, "Each sovereign serves Heaven and Earth according to his own ritual system; those who today rely on isolated passages from the Rites of Zhou as the great framework of state governance fear being narrow and not knowing how to expand.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Su, Attendant Cavalier at Large, argued: "Each king serves Heaven and Earth according to his own ritual system. Those who now treat isolated passages from the Rites of Zhou as the foundation of state governance risk being cramped in vision and failing to grasp the broader principle.

sentences.zh: 漢武帝東巡封禪還，祠太一于甘泉，祭后土于汾陰，皆盡用其樂。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wu of Han returned from his eastern tour and feng-shan rites, he sacrificed to the Grand One at Ganquan and to Hou Tu at Fenyin—all fully employed their music.
translations.idiomatic: After Emperor Wu of Han returned from his eastern tour and the feng-shan rites, he sacrificed to the Grand One at Ganquan and to Hou Tu at Fenyin, employing the full musical establishment on both occasions.

sentences.zh: 言盡用者，為盡用宮縣之樂也。

translations.literal: When it says 'fully employed,' it means fully employing the suspended bell music.
translations.idiomatic: The phrase 'fully employed' means the full use of suspended bell music.

sentences.zh: 天地之性貴質者，盖謂其器之不文爾，不謂庶物當復減之也。

translations.literal: That Heaven and Earth value simplicity means their vessels are unfashioned—not that all things should be further reduced.
translations.idiomatic: That Heaven and Earth value simplicity refers to their vessels being plain and unadorned, not to reducing everything else still further.

sentences.zh: 禮，天子宮縣，舞八佾。

translations.literal: In ritual, the Son of Heaven has suspended bells and dances eight rows.
translations.idiomatic: By ritual, the Son of Heaven employs suspended bells and an eight-row dance.

sentences.zh: 今祀圓丘方澤，宜以天子制，設宮縣之樂，八佾之舞。

translations.literal: Now in sacrificing at the Round Mound and Square Pond, one should use the Son of Heaven's regimen, setting up suspended bell music and eight-row dance.
translations.idiomatic: Sacrifices at the Round Mound and Square Pond should follow the Son of Heaven's standard, with suspended bell music and an eight-row dance.

sentences.zh: 」衛臻、繆襲、左延年等咸同肅議。

translations.literal: " Wei Zhen, Miao Xi, Zuo Yannian, and others all agreed with Su's proposal.
translations.idiomatic: " Wei Zhen, Miao Xi, Zuo Yannian, and others all concurred with Wang Su's proposal.

sentences.zh: 奏可。

translations.literal: The memorial was approved.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial was approved.

sentences.zh: 肅又議曰：「說者以為周家祀天，唯舞《雲門》；

translations.literal: Su again argued, saying, "Some hold that when the Zhou sacrificed to Heaven they danced only the Cloud Gate;
translations.idiomatic: Wang Su argued further: "Some maintain that when the Zhou sacrificed to Heaven they danced only the Cloud Gate;

sentences.zh: 祭地，唯舞《咸池》；

translations.literal: when they sacrificed to Earth, only the Xian Chi;
translations.idiomatic: when they sacrificed to Earth, only the Xian Chi;

translations.literal: in the ancestral temple, only the Grand Martial—this seems to miss the meaning.
translations.idiomatic: and in the ancestral temple, only the Grand Martial—this seems to misunderstand the principle.

sentences.zh: 周禮賓客皆作備樂。

translations.literal: In the Rites of Zhou, for guests all complete music is performed.
translations.idiomatic: In the Rites of Zhou, guests were entertained with the full musical repertoire.

sentences.zh: 《左傳》：『王子穨享五大夫樂及徧舞。

translations.literal: The Zuo Commentary: "Prince Zi Tui entertained five grand officers with music through to the complete dances.
translations.idiomatic: The Zuo Commentary records: "Prince Zi Tui entertained five grand officers with music through to the full round of dances.

sentences.zh: 』六代之樂也。

translations.literal: " It was the music of six generations.
translations.idiomatic: " This was the music of six dynasties.

sentences.zh: 然則一會之日，具作六代樂矣。

translations.literal: Thus on a single day's gathering, all six generations of music were fully performed.
translations.idiomatic: On a single day's assembly, then, all six generations of music were performed in full.

sentences.zh: 天地宗廟，事之大者，賓客燕會，比之為細。

translations.literal: Heaven, Earth, and the ancestral temple are the greatest affairs; guest banquets and feasts are trivial by comparison.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven, Earth, and the ancestral temple are the weightiest rites; guest banquets and feasts are minor by comparison.

sentences.zh: 《王制》曰：『庶羞不踰牲，燕衣不踰祭服。

translations.literal: The Royal Regulations say: "Ordinary viands do not exceed sacrificial victims; banquet robes do not exceed sacrificial robes.
translations.idiomatic: The Royal Regulations state: "Everyday dishes do not surpass sacrificial victims, and banquet garments do not surpass sacrificial robes.

sentences.zh: 』可以燕樂而踰天地宗廟之樂乎？

translations.literal: " Can one use feast music to exceed the music of Heaven, Earth, and the ancestral temple?
translations.idiomatic: " How then can feast music be allowed to surpass the music of Heaven, Earth, and the ancestral temple?

sentences.zh: 《周官》：『以六律、六呂、五聲、八音、六舞大合樂，以致鬼神，以和邦國，以諧萬民，以安賓客，以說遠人。

translations.literal: The Rites of Zhou: "With the six pitches, six tubes, five tones, eight instruments, and six dances one grandly combines music to summon spirits and ghosts, harmonize the states, tune the myriad people, settle guests, and please distant peoples.
translations.idiomatic: The Rites of Zhou say: "With the six pitches, six tubes, five tones, eight instruments, and six dances one combines music on the grand scale—to summon spirits and ghosts, harmonize the states, tune the myriad people, put guests at ease, and delight distant peoples.

sentences.zh: 』夫六律、六呂、五聲、八音，皆一時而作之，至於六舞獨分擘而用之，所以不懕人心也。

translations.literal: " The six pitches, six tubes, five tones, and eight instruments are all produced at one time; only the six dances are separately divided and deployed—so as not to surfeit people's hearts.
translations.idiomatic: " The six pitches, six tubes, five tones, and eight instruments are all performed together at once; only the six dances are separately apportioned and used, so as not to overwhelm the audience.

sentences.zh: 又《周官》：『韎師掌教韎樂，祭祀則帥其屬而舞之，大享亦如之。

translations.literal: Again the Rites of Zhou: "The Miao master supervises teaching Miao music; at sacrifices he leads his subordinates in dancing it, and at grand feasts it is the same.
translations.idiomatic: The Rites of Zhou also say: "The Miao master oversees instruction in Miao music; at sacrifices he leads his subordinates in dancing it, and the same holds for grand feasts.

sentences.zh: 』韎，東夷之樂也。

translations.literal: " Miao is the music of the eastern Yi.
translations.idiomatic: " Miao was the music of the eastern Yi.

sentences.zh: 又：『鞮鞻氏掌四夷之樂與其聲歌，祭祀則次而歌之，燕亦如之。

translations.literal: Again: "The Di Li clan supervises the music of the four barbarians and their songs; at sacrifices they are ranked and sung; at banquets it is likewise.
translations.idiomatic: Again: "The Di Li clan oversees the music of the four barbarians and their songs; at sacrifices these are performed in sequence, and banquets follow the same practice.

sentences.zh: 』四夷之樂，乃入宗廟；

translations.literal: " Music of the four barbarians entered the ancestral temple;
translations.idiomatic: " Music of the four barbarians was admitted into the ancestral temple;

sentences.zh: 先代之典，獨不得用。

translations.literal: while the classics of former ages alone could not be used?
translations.idiomatic: yet the classics of former ages alone could not be used?

sentences.zh: 大享及燕日如之者，明古今夷、夏之樂，皆主之於宗廟，而後播及其餘也。

translations.literal: That grand feasts and banquets did the same shows that ancient and modern barbarian and Chinese music alike took the ancestral temple as their center, then spread to the rest.
translations.idiomatic: That grand feasts and banquets followed the same pattern shows that music of both barbarian and Chinese origin, ancient and modern, took the ancestral temple as its center and only then spread elsewhere.

sentences.zh: 夫作先王樂者，貴能包而用之；

translations.literal: Those who compose the music of former kings value being able to encompass and use it;
translations.idiomatic: In performing the music of former kings, the point is to encompass it and put it to use;

sentences.zh: 納四夷之樂者，美德廣之所及也。

translations.literal: to admit the music of the four barbarians is the reach of broad virtue.
translations.idiomatic: to admit the music of the four barbarians is the mark of far-reaching virtue.

sentences.zh: 高皇帝、大皇帝、太祖、高祖、文昭廟，皆宜兼用先代及《武始》、《太鈞》之舞。

translations.literal: The temples of the High Emperor, Grand Emperor, Founding Emperor, Elevated Ancestor, and Wen Zhao should all suitably combine use of music of former ages and the dances Wu Shi and Tai Jun.
translations.idiomatic: The temples of the High Emperor, Grand Emperor, Founding Emperor, Elevated Ancestor, and Wen Zhao should all employ both music of former ages and the Wu Shi and Tai Jun dances.

sentences.zh: 」有司奏：「宜如肅議。

translations.literal: " The relevant offices memorialized: "It should accord with Su's proposal.
translations.idiomatic: " The responsible offices memorialized: "The proposal should follow Wang Su's recommendation.

sentences.zh: 」奏可。

translations.literal: " The memorial was approved.
translations.idiomatic: " The memorial was approved.

sentences.zh: 肅私造宗廟詩頌十二篇，不被歌。

translations.literal: Su privately composed twelve temple hymn and eulogy pieces, but they were not sung.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Su privately composed twelve temple hymns and eulogies, but they were never performed.

sentences.zh: 晉武帝太始二年，改制郊廟歌，其樂舞亦仍舊也。

translations.literal: In the second year of Taishi, Emperor Wu of Jin reformed the suburban and temple songs; the music and dances remained as before.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Taishi, Emperor Wu of Jin reformed the suburban and temple songs, but the music and dances themselves remained unchanged.

sentences.zh: 漢光武平隴、蜀，增廣郊祀，高皇帝配食，樂奏《青陽》、《朱明》、《西皓》、《玄冥》、《雲翹》、《育命》之舞。

translations.literal: When Guangwu of Han pacified Long and Shu, he expanded suburban sacrifices; the High Emperor received paired offerings, and music played the dances Qing Yang, Zhu Ming, Xi Hao, Xuan Ming, Yun Qiao, and Yu Ming.
translations.idiomatic: After Guangwu of Han pacified Long and Shu, he expanded the suburban sacrifices. The High Emperor received paired offerings, and the dances Qing Yang, Zhu Ming, Xi Hao, Xuan Ming, Yun Qiao, and Yu Ming were performed.

sentences.zh: 北郊及祀明堂，並奏樂如南郊。

translations.literal: At the northern suburb and in sacrificing at the Bright Hall, music was performed alike to the southern suburb.
translations.idiomatic: At the northern suburb and at sacrifices in the Bright Hall, the same music was performed as at the southern suburb.

sentences.zh: 迎時氣五郊：春歌《青陽》，夏歌《朱明》，並舞《雲翹》之舞；

translations.literal: At the five suburbs welcoming seasonal qi: spring sang Qing Yang, summer sang Zhu Ming, both dancing Yun Qiao;
translations.idiomatic: At the five suburban rites welcoming the seasonal qi, spring sang Qing Yang and summer sang Zhu Ming, both accompanied by the Yun Qiao dance;

sentences.zh: 秋歌《西皓》，冬歌《玄冥》，並舞《育命》之舞；

translations.literal: autumn sang Xi Hao, winter sang Xuan Ming, both dancing Yu Ming;
translations.idiomatic: autumn sang Xi Hao and winter sang Xuan Ming, both accompanied by the Yu Ming dance;

sentences.zh: 夏季歌《朱明》，兼舞二舞。

translations.literal: in the summer season they sang Zhu Ming and performed both dances.
translations.idiomatic: in summer they sang Zhu Ming and performed both dances together.

sentences.zh: 章帝元和二年，宗廟樂，故事，食舉有《鹿鳴》、《承元氣》二曲。

translations.literal: In the second year of Yuanhe of Emperor Zhang, for ancestral temple music, by precedent the meal-accompaniment had two pieces: Deer Call and Receiving Primordial Qi.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Yuanhe under Emperor Zhang, ancestral temple music by precedent included two meal-accompaniment pieces: Deer Call and Receiving Primordial Qi.

sentences.zh: 三年，自作詩四篇，一曰《思齊皇姚》，二曰《六騏驎》，三曰《竭肅雝》，四曰《陟叱根》。

translations.literal: In the third year he personally composed four poems: first, Si Qi Huang Yao; second, Liu Qi Lin; third, Jie Su Yong; fourth, Zhi Chi Gen.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he composed four poems himself: Si Qi Huang Yao, Liu Qi Lin, Jie Su Yong, and Zhi Chi Gen.

sentences.zh: 合前六曲，以為宗廟食舉。

translations.literal: Together with the previous six pieces, these became the ancestral temple meal-accompaniment.
translations.idiomatic: Combined with the previous six pieces, these formed the ancestral temple meal-accompaniment.

sentences.zh: 加宗廟食舉《重來》、《上陵》二曲，合八曲為上陵食舉。

translations.literal: Adding to ancestral temple meal-accompaniment Come Again and Ascending the Mound, eight pieces became the Shang-ling meal-accompaniment.
translations.idiomatic: Come Again and Ascending the Mound were added to the ancestral temple meal-accompaniment, making eight pieces in all for the Shang-ling meal-accompaniment.

sentences.zh: 減宗廟食舉《承元氣》一曲，加《惟天之命》、《天之歷數》二曲，合七曲為殿中御食飯舉。

translations.literal: Removing one piece, Receiving Primordial Qi, from ancestral temple meal-accompaniment and adding Mandate of Heaven and Heaven's Succession, seven pieces became the palace meal-accompaniment.
translations.idiomatic: Receiving Primordial Qi was removed from the ancestral temple meal-accompaniment, and Mandate of Heaven and Heaven's Succession were added, making seven pieces for the palace meal-accompaniment.

sentences.zh: 又漢太樂食舉十三曲：一曰《鹿鳴》，二曰《重來》，三曰《初造》，四曰《俠安》，五曰《歸來》，六曰《遠期》，七曰《有所思》，八曰《明星》，九曰《清涼》，十曰《涉大海》，十一曰《大置酒》，十二曰《承元氣》，十三曰《海淡淡》。

translations.literal: Also, the Han Grand Music meal-accompaniment had thirteen pieces: first, Deer Call; second, Come Again; third, First Creation; fourth, Gallant Peace; fifth, Return; sixth, Far Horizon; seventh, I Have Someone in Mind; eighth, Bright Star; ninth, Clear Coolness; tenth, Crossing the Great Sea; eleventh, Great Wine Feast; twelfth, Receiving Primordial Qi; thirteenth, Vast Sea.
translations.idiomatic: The Han Grand Music meal-accompaniment comprised thirteen pieces: Deer Call, Come Again, First Creation, Gallant Peace, Return, Far Horizon, I Have Someone in Mind, Bright Star, Clear Coolness, Crossing the Great Sea, Great Wine Feast, Receiving Primordial Qi, and Vast Sea.

sentences.zh: 魏氏及晉荀勗、傅玄並為歌辭。

translations.literal: The Wei and Jin—Xun Xu and Fu Xuan—both wrote lyrics.
translations.idiomatic: Under Wei and Jin, Xun Xu and Fu Xuan both composed new lyrics.

sentences.zh: 魏時以《遠期》、《承元氣》、《海淡淡》三曲多不通利，省之。

translations.literal: Under Wei, three pieces—Far Horizon, Receiving Primordial Qi, and Vast Sea—were often awkward and were cut.
translations.idiomatic: Under Wei, Far Horizon, Receiving Primordial Qi, and Vast Sea were often awkward to perform and were dropped.

sentences.zh: 魏雅樂四曲：一曰《鹿鳴》，後改曰《於赫》，詠武帝；

translations.literal: Wei elegant music had four pieces: first, Deer Call, later changed to Majestic, praising Emperor Wu;
translations.idiomatic: Wei elegant music comprised four pieces: Deer Call, later renamed Majestic in praise of Emperor Wu;

sentences.zh: 二曰《騶虞》，後改曰《巍巍》，詠文帝；

translations.literal: second, Zou Yu, later changed to Lofty, praising Emperor Wen;
translations.idiomatic: Zou Yu, later renamed Lofty in praise of Emperor Wen;

sentences.zh: 三曰《伐檀》，後省除；

translations.literal: third, Felling Sandalwood, later cut;
translations.idiomatic: Felling Sandalwood, later dropped;

sentences.zh: 四曰《文王》，後改曰《洋洋》，詠明帝。

translations.literal: fourth, King Wen, later changed to Abundant, praising Emperor Ming.
translations.idiomatic: and King Wen, later renamed Abundant in praise of Emperor Ming.

sentences.zh: 《騶虞》、《伐檀》、《文王》並左延年改其聲。

translations.literal: Zou Yu, Felling Sandalwood, and King Wen—all had their melodies altered by Zuo Yannian.
translations.idiomatic: Zuo Yannian revised the melodies of Zou Yu, Felling Sandalwood, and King Wen.

sentences.zh: 正旦大會，太尉奉璧，羣后行禮，東廂雅樂郎作者是也。

translations.literal: At the New Year's great assembly, when the Grand Commandant presented the jade disk and the feudal lords performed the rite, this is what the elegant music masters of the eastern side composed.
translations.idiomatic: These were composed by the elegant music masters of the eastern side for the New Year's great assembly, when the Grand Commandant presented the jade disk and the feudal lords performed the rite.

sentences.zh: 今謂之行禮曲，姑洗廂所奏。

translations.literal: Today it is called the Rite-Processional music, played from the Gu Xian side.
translations.idiomatic: It is now called the Rite-Processional music and is performed from the Gu Xian side.

sentences.zh: 案：《鹿鳴》本以宴樂為體，無當於朝享，往時之失也。

translations.literal: Note: Deer Call was originally a banquet piece; it had no place at court audience—an error of former times.
translations.idiomatic: It should be noted that Deer Call was originally a banquet piece and had no proper place at court audience—a mistake of earlier practice.

sentences.zh: 晉武泰始五年，尚書奏使太僕傅玄、中書監荀勗、黃門侍郎張華各造正旦行禮及王公上壽酒食舉樂歌詩。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Taishi under Jin Wu, the Ministerial Court memorialized that the Grand Steward Fu Xuan, Director of the Secretariat Xun Xu, and Yellow Gate Attendant Zhang Hua should each compose New Year's rite-processional and princely birthday wine meal-accompaniment music and lyrics.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Taishi, the Ministerial Court proposed that Fu Xuan, Grand Steward; Xun Xu, Director of the Secretariat; and Zhang Hua, Yellow Gate Attendant, each compose music and lyrics for the New Year's rite-processional and for the princes' birthday wine and meal-accompaniment.

sentences.zh: 詔又使中書郎成公綏亦作。

translations.literal: An edict also ordered Secretariat Gentleman Cheng Gong Sui to compose as well.
translations.idiomatic: An edict also directed Secretariat Gentleman Cheng Gong Sui to compose pieces.

sentences.zh: 張華表曰：「按魏上壽食舉詩及漢氏所施用，其文句長短不齊，未皆合古。

translations.literal: Zhang Hua submitted, saying, "Examining the Wei birthday meal-accompaniment poems and those used by Han, their lines vary in length and do not all accord with antiquity.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Hua submitted a memorial: "Reviewing the Wei birthday meal-accompaniment poems and those used under Han, their lines vary in length and do not all conform to ancient practice.

sentences.zh: 葢以依詠弦節，本有因循，而識樂知音，足以制聲度曲法用，率非凡近所能改。

translations.literal: This is because they follow the rhythm of string accompaniment and inherit established practice; those who know music and understand tones can set sound and measure melody by rule—ordinarily not what ordinary men of the day can alter.
translations.idiomatic: This is because they follow the rhythms of string accompaniment and inherit long-established practice. Only those who truly know music can set pitches and measure melodies by rule—work that ordinary men of the day cannot readily change.

sentences.zh: 二代三京，襲而不變，雖詩章詞異，興廢隨時，至其韻逗曲折，皆繫於舊有由然也。

translations.literal: Across two dynasties and three capitals, they were inherited unchanged; though the poems' wording differed and pieces rose and fell with the times, their cadences and turns all depended on what had existed before—there was reason for this.
translations.idiomatic: Across two dynasties and three capitals the forms were handed down unchanged. Though the wording of the poems differed and pieces were added or dropped with the times, their cadences and turns all depended on what had gone before, and for good reason.

sentences.zh: 是以一皆因就，不敢有所改易。

translations.literal: Therefore I have followed them entirely and dare make no changes.
translations.idiomatic: For this reason I followed the existing forms throughout and did not venture to alter them.

sentences.zh: 」荀勗則曰：「魏氏歌詩，或二言，或三言，或四言，或五言，與古詩不類。

translations.literal: " Xun Xu, however, said, "Wei song-poems are sometimes two-word, sometimes three-word, sometimes four-word, sometimes five-word—they do not resemble ancient poetry.
translations.idiomatic: " Xun Xu, by contrast, argued: "Wei song-poems use lines of two, three, four, or five words—they do not resemble ancient poetry.

sentences.zh: 」以問司律中郎將陳頎，頎曰：「被之金石，未必皆當。

translations.literal: " He asked Director of Pitch Regulation Chen Yi, who said, "When set to bells and stones, not all necessarily fit.
translations.idiomatic: " He consulted Chen Yi, Director of Pitch Regulation, who replied: "When matched to bells and stones, not all of them necessarily fit.

sentences.zh: 」故勗造晉歌，皆為四言，唯王公上壽酒一篇為三言五言，此則華、勗所明異旨也。

translations.literal: " Therefore Xu composed Jin songs all in four-word lines, except one princely birthday wine piece in three- and five-word lines—this is where Hua and Xu clearly differed in intent.
translations.idiomatic: " Xu therefore composed Jin songs entirely in four-word lines, except for one princely birthday wine piece in three- and five-word lines—this was the clear difference in approach between Zhang Hua and Xun Xu.

sentences.zh: 九年，荀勗遂典知樂事，使郭夏、宋識等造《正德》《大豫》之舞，而勗及傅玄、張華又各造此舞歌詩。

translations.literal: In the ninth year, Xun Xu took charge of music affairs, had Guo Xia, Song Shi, and others create the Zheng De and Da Yu dances, and Xu together with Fu Xuan and Zhang Hua each composed lyrics for these dances.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year Xun Xu assumed charge of music affairs. He had Guo Xia, Song Shi, and others create the Zheng De and Da Yu dances, while Xu, Fu Xuan, and Zhang Hua each composed lyrics for them.

sentences.zh: 勗作新律笛十二枚，散騎常侍阮咸譏新律聲高，高近哀思，不合中和。

translations.literal: Xu made twelve new pitch-standard flutes; Ruan Xian, Attendant Cavalier at Large, criticized the new pitches as too high—too close to mournful longing and not conforming to harmonious moderation.
translations.idiomatic: Xu made twelve new pitch-standard flutes. Ruan Xian, Attendant Cavalier at Large, criticized the new pitches as too high—too close to mournful longing and out of keeping with harmonious moderation.

sentences.zh: 勗以為異己，出咸為始平相。

translations.literal: Xu regarded him as opposing himself and sent Xian out as Administrator of Shiping.
translations.idiomatic: Xu took this as personal opposition and had Xian posted out as Administrator of Shiping.

sentences.zh: 晉又改魏《昭武舞》曰《宣武舞》，《羽籥舞》曰《宣文舞》。

translations.literal: Jin also changed Wei's Zhao Wu dance to Xuan Wu dance and the Yu Yue dance to Xuan Wen dance.
translations.idiomatic: Jin also renamed Wei's Zhao Wu dance as Xuan Wu and the Yu Yue dance as Xuan Wen.

sentences.zh: 咸寧元年，詔定祖宗之號，而廟樂同用《正德》《大豫》之舞。

translations.literal: In the first year of Xianning, an edict fixed the titles of the imperial ancestors, and temple music uniformly used the Zheng De and Da Yu dances.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Xianning, an edict fixed the titles of the imperial ancestors, and temple music uniformly employed the Zheng De and Da Yu dances.

sentences.zh: 至江左初立宗廟，尚書下太常祭祀所用樂名，太常賀循答云：「魏氏增損漢樂以為一代之禮，未審大晉樂名所以為異。

translations.literal: When the Eastern Court first established the ancestral temple, the Ministerial Court forwarded to the Grand Master of Ceremonies the names of music used in sacrifice; Grand Master He Xun replied, saying, "Wei added to and reduced Han music to form the rites of one dynasty; it is not clear why Great Jin's music names differ.
translations.idiomatic: When the Eastern Court first established the ancestral temple, the Ministerial Court asked the Grand Master of Ceremonies for the names of music used in sacrifice. He Xun replied: "Wei had added to and trimmed Han music to form the rites of its dynasty; it is unclear why Great Jin's music names should differ.

sentences.zh: 遭離喪亂，舊典不存，然此諸樂，皆和之以鐘律，文之以五聲，詠之於歌詞，陳之於舞列，宮縣在下，琴瑟在堂，八音迭奏，雅樂並作，登歌下管，各有常詠，周人之舊也。

translations.literal: Having suffered turmoil and disorder, the old canon no longer survives; yet all this music is harmonized with bells and pitch pipes, patterned with the five tones, chanted in lyrics, arrayed in dance formations—suspended bells below, zithers and lutes in the hall, the eight sounds played in succession, elegant music performed together, ascending song and descending pipes each with fixed chants: this is the Zhou people's ancient practice.
translations.idiomatic: After the turmoil of exile and war the old canon no longer survives. Yet this music was harmonized with bells and pitch pipes, shaped by the five tones, sung in lyrics, and displayed in dance formations—suspended bells below, zithers and lutes in the hall, the eight sounds played in succession, elegant music performed together, ascending song and descending pipes each with fixed chants. This was the ancient practice of the Zhou.

sentences.zh: 自漢氏以來，依放此禮，自造新詩而已。

translations.literal: Since Han, they have followed this ritual and merely composed new poems themselves.
translations.idiomatic: Since Han, each dynasty has followed this ritual framework and simply composed new poems of its own.

sentences.zh: 舊京荒廢，今既散亡，音韻曲折，又無識者，則於今難以意言。

translations.literal: The old capital lies in ruin; now that it is scattered and lost, and with no one who knows the turns of tone and pitch, it is hard to speak of by intention today.
translations.idiomatic: The old capital lies in ruins, and what survives is scattered and lost. With no one left who knows the turns of tone and pitch, it is impossible to reconstruct the details today.

sentences.zh: 」于時以無雅樂器及伶人，省太樂并鼓吹令。

translations.literal: " At the time, because there were no elegant music instruments or performers, the offices of Grand Music and Processional Drums were abolished.
translations.idiomatic: " At the time, lacking elegant music instruments and performers, the offices of Grand Music and Processional Drums were abolished.

sentences.zh: 是後頗得登歌，食舉之樂，猶有未備。

translations.literal: After this they somewhat recovered ascending song, but meal-accompaniment music was still incomplete.
translations.idiomatic: Afterward ascending song was partly recovered, but meal-accompaniment music remained incomplete.

sentences.zh: 明帝太寧末，又詔阮孚等增益之。

translations.literal: At the end of Taining under Emperor Ming, an edict again had Ruan Fu and others augment it.
translations.idiomatic: Near the end of Taining under Emperor Ming, an edict directed Ruan Fu and others to expand the repertoire further.

sentences.zh: 成帝咸和中，乃復置太樂官，鳩集遺逸，而尚未有金石也。

translations.literal: In Xianhe under Emperor Cheng, the Grand Music office was restored, lost pieces were gathered together, but bells and stones were still lacking.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Cheng in the Xianhe era, the Grand Music office was restored and scattered pieces were gathered together, but bells and stones were still unavailable.

sentences.zh: 初，荀勗既以新律造二舞，又更修正鐘磬，事未竟而勗薨。

translations.literal: Initially, after Xun Xu had used the new pitch standards to create the two dances, he also began revising bells and chime-stones; the work was unfinished when Xu died.
translations.idiomatic: Initially, after Xun Xu used the new pitch standards to create the two dances, he also began revising the bells and chime-stones, but the work was unfinished when he died.

sentences.zh: 惠帝元康三年，詔其子黃門侍郎蕃修定金石，以施郊廟。

translations.literal: In the third year of Yuankang under Emperor Hui, an edict ordered his son, Yellow Gate Attendant Fan, to revise and fix the bells and stones for use at suburban and temple rites.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Yuankang under Emperor Hui, an edict directed Xu's son Fan, Yellow Gate Attendant, to revise the bells and stones for use at suburban and temple rites.

sentences.zh: 尋值喪亂，遺聲舊制，莫有記者。

translations.literal: Soon turmoil struck; the transmitted sounds and old system had no record-keeper.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward turmoil struck, and no records survived of the transmitted sounds and old system.

sentences.zh: 庾亮為荊州，與謝尚共為朝廷修雅樂，亮尋薨。

translations.literal: When Yu Liang was in Jing Province, he and Xie Shang together restored elegant music for the court; Liang soon died.
translations.idiomatic: While Yu Liang governed Jing Province, he and Xie Shang worked together to restore elegant music for the court, but Liang soon died.

sentences.zh: 庾翼、桓溫專事軍旅，樂器在庫，遂至朽壞焉。

translations.literal: Yu Yi and Huan Wen devoted themselves to military campaigns; the instruments lay in storehouses and eventually rotted away.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Yi and Huan Wen devoted themselves to military campaigns, and the instruments stored in the warehouses eventually rotted away.

sentences.zh: 晉氏之亂也，樂人悉沒戎虜。

translations.literal: During the disorder of the Jin house, all musicians were lost to barbarian captivity.
translations.idiomatic: During the Jin dynasty's collapse, all musicians were lost to barbarian captivity.

sentences.zh: 及胡亡，鄴下樂人，頗有來者。

translations.literal: When the Hu regime fell, quite a few musicians from Ye returned.
translations.idiomatic: After the Hu regime fell, a number of musicians from Ye made their way back.

sentences.zh: 謝尚時為尚書僕射，因之以具鐘磬。

translations.literal: Xie Shang was then Vice Director of the Ministerial Court and on this basis assembled bells and chime-stones.
translations.idiomatic: Xie Shang, then Vice Director of the Ministerial Court, used them to assemble a full set of bells and chime-stones.

sentences.zh: 太元中，破符堅，又獲樂工楊蜀等，閑練舊樂，於是四廂金石始備焉。

translations.literal: In the Taiyuan era, after defeating Fu Jian, they also captured musicians Yang Shu and others, who practiced the old music at leisure; thus bells and stones for all four sides were first completed.
translations.idiomatic: In the Taiyuan era, after the defeat of Fu Jian, musicians including Yang Shu were captured and practiced the old music at leisure. Only then were bells and chime-stones completed for all four sides.

sentences.zh: 宋文帝元嘉九年，大樂令鍾宗之更調金石。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Yuanjia under Emperor Wen of Song, Grand Music Director Zhong Zongzhi retuned the bells and stones.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year of Yuanjia under Emperor Wen of Song, Grand Music Director Zhong Zongzhi retuned the bells and stones.

sentences.zh: 十四年，治書令史奚縱又改之。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year, Document Drafting Clerk Xi Zong changed them again.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year, Document Drafting Clerk Xi Zong revised them again.

sentences.zh: 語在《律歷志》。

translations.literal: The account is in the Treatise on Pitch Pipes and the Calendar.
translations.idiomatic: The details are recorded in the Treatise on Pitch Pipes and the Calendar.

sentences.zh: 晉世曹毗、王珣等亦增造宗廟歌詩，然郊祀遂不設樂。

translations.literal: In Jin times Cao Pi, Wang Xun, and others also added ancestral temple song-poems, yet suburban sacrifice thereafter had no music installed.
translations.idiomatic: In Jin times Cao Pi, Wang Xun, and others also composed additional ancestral temple songs, yet suburban sacrifices thereafter went without music.

sentences.zh: 何承天曰：「世咸傳吳朝無雅樂。

translations.literal: He Chengtian said, "The world widely reports that the Wu court had no elegant music.
translations.idiomatic: He Chengtian observed: "It is widely said that the Wu court had no elegant music.

sentences.zh: 案孫皓迎父喪明陵，唯云倡伎晝夜不息，則無金石登歌可知矣。

translations.literal: Examining Sun Hao's reception of his father's coffin at Mingling, it mentions only singers and performers day and night without cease—then the absence of bells, stones, and ascending song is clear.
translations.idiomatic: Examining Sun Hao's reception of his father's coffin at Mingling, the record mentions only singers and performers day and night without cease—the absence of bells, stones, and ascending song is evident.

sentences.zh: 」承天曰：「或云今之《神絃》，孫氏以為宗廟登歌也。

translations.literal: " Chengtian said, "Some say that today's Divine Strings was used by the Sun house as ancestral temple ascending song.
translations.idiomatic: " He Chengtian added: "Some hold that today's Divine Strings was used by the Sun house as ancestral temple ascending song.

sentences.zh: 」史臣案：陸機《孫權誄》「《肆夏》在廟，《雲翹》承機，不容虛設」此言。

translations.literal: " The historiographer notes: Lu Ji's Eulogy for Sun Quan says, "Si Xia in the temple, Yun Qiao continuing the occasion—they cannot have been set up in vain"—this statement.
translations.idiomatic: " The historiographer comments: Lu Ji's Eulogy for Sun Quan states, "Si Xia in the temple, Yun Qiao continuing the occasion—they cannot have been set up in vain."

sentences.zh: 又韋昭孫休世上《鼓吹鐃歌》十二曲表曰：「當付樂官善歌者習歌。

translations.literal: Also, Wei Zhao's memorial on the twelve Drum-and-Chime Processional pieces of Sun Xiu's reign says, "They should be given to music officials skilled in singing to learn and perform.
translations.idiomatic: Also, Wei Zhao's memorial on the twelve Drum-and-Chime Processional pieces from Sun Xiu's reign states: "They should be entrusted to music officials skilled in singing to learn and perform.

sentences.zh: 」然則吳朝非無樂官，善歌者乃能以歌辭被絲管，寧容止以《神絃》為廟樂而已乎？

translations.literal: " Then the Wu court was not without music officials; skilled singers could set lyrics to string and pipe—how could one accept only Divine Strings as temple music?
translations.idiomatic: " This shows the Wu court did have music officials, and skilled singers could set lyrics to string and wind instruments. How could temple music have consisted of nothing but Divine Strings?

sentences.zh: 孝建二年九月甲午，有司奏：「前殿中曹郎荀萬秋議：按禮，祭天地有樂者，為降神也。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, on the jiawu day, of the second year of Xiaojian, the relevant offices memorialized: "Former Palace Bureau Gentleman Xun Wanqiu argued: According to ritual, music at sacrifices to Heaven and Earth exists to summon the spirits downward.
translations.idiomatic: On the jiawu day of the ninth month in the second year of Xiaojian, the relevant offices memorialized: "Former Palace Bureau Gentleman Xun Wanqiu argued that by ritual, music at sacrifices to Heaven and Earth serves to summon the spirits downward.

sentences.zh: 故《易》曰：『雷出地奮豫。

translations.literal: Therefore the Book of Changes says: "Thunder emerges from the earth in vigorous Yu.
translations.idiomatic: The Book of Changes therefore says: "Thunder emerges from the earth in the hexagram Yu.

sentences.zh: 先王以作樂崇德，殷薦之上帝，以配祖考。

translations.literal: The former kings made music to exalt virtue; in the Yu sacrifice they presented to the Supreme Lord, pairing with the founding ancestors.
translations.idiomatic: The former kings made music to exalt virtue; in the Yu sacrifice they presented offerings to the Supreme Lord, paired with the founding ancestors.

sentences.zh: 』《周官》曰：『作樂於圜丘之上，天神皆降。

translations.literal: " The Rites of Zhou says: "Make music atop the Round Mound, and the celestial spirits all descend.
translations.idiomatic: " The Rites of Zhou states: "Make music atop the Round Mound, and the celestial spirits all descend.

sentences.zh: 作樂於方澤之中，地祗皆出。

translations.literal: Make music within the Square Pond, and the earthly spirits all emerge.
translations.idiomatic: Make music within the Square Pond, and the earthly spirits all emerge.

sentences.zh: 』又曰：『乃奏黃鐘，歌大呂，舞《雲門》，以祀天神。

translations.literal: " Again it says: "Then play the yellow bell, sing the great tube, dance the Cloud Gate, to sacrifice to the celestial spirits.
translations.idiomatic: " It also says: "Then play the yellow bell, sing the great tube, dance the Cloud Gate, to sacrifice to the celestial spirits.

sentences.zh: 乃奏大簇，歌應鐘，舞《咸池》，以祀地祗。

translations.literal: Then play the great cluster, sing the responding bell, dance the Xian Chi, to sacrifice to the earthly spirits.
translations.idiomatic: Then play the great cluster, sing the responding bell, dance the Xian Chi, to sacrifice to the earthly spirits.

sentences.zh: 』由斯而言，以樂祭天地，其來尚矣。

translations.literal: " From this it follows that using music to sacrifice to Heaven and Earth has ancient origins.
translations.idiomatic: " From this it is clear that using music in sacrifices to Heaven and Earth is of long standing.

sentences.zh: 今郊享闕樂，竊以為疑。

translations.literal: Now suburban sacrifice lacks music—I venture to find this doubtful.
translations.idiomatic: Yet suburban sacrifice now lacks music, which I find troubling.

sentences.zh: 《祭統》曰：『夫祭有三重焉，獻之屬，莫重於祼，聲莫重於升歌，舞莫重於《武宿夜》，此周道也。

translations.literal: The Record of Sacrifice says: "Sacrifice has three weightiest elements among the offerings: none weightier than the libation; among sounds, none weightier than ascending song; among dances, none weightier than Martial Night Vigil—this was the Zhou way.
translations.idiomatic: The Record of Sacrifice states: "Among sacrificial offerings, nothing is weightier than the libation; among sounds, nothing is weightier than ascending song; among dances, nothing is weightier than Martial Night Vigil—this was the Zhou way.

sentences.zh: 』至於秦奏《五行》，魏舞《咸熙》，皆以用享。

translations.literal: " As for Qin performing the Five Elements, Wei dancing Xian Xi—all were used in sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: " Qin performed the Five Elements, Wei danced Xian Xi—all were used in sacrificial rites.

sentences.zh: 爰逮晉氏，泰始之初，傅玄作晉郊廟歌詩三十二篇。

translations.literal: Down to the Jin house, at the start of Taishi, Fu Xuan composed thirty-two Jin suburban and temple song-poems.
translations.idiomatic: Down to the Jin dynasty, at the beginning of Taishi, Fu Xuan composed thirty-two suburban and temple song-poems for Jin.

sentences.zh: 元康中，荀蕃受詔成父勗業，金石四縣，用之郊廟。

translations.literal: In Yuankang, Xun Fan received an edict to complete his father Xu's work; bells, stones, and four bell-sets were used at suburban and temple rites.
translations.idiomatic: During Yuankang, Xun Fan received an edict to complete his father Xu's work; bells, stones, and four bell-sets were deployed at suburban and temple rites.

sentences.zh: 是則相承郊廟有樂之證也。

translations.literal: This is proof handed down that suburban and temple rites had music.
translations.idiomatic: This is transmitted proof that suburban and temple rites included music.

sentences.zh: 今廟祀登歌雖奏，而象舞未陳，懼闕備禮。

translations.literal: Now at temple sacrifice ascending song is performed, yet the symbolic dance is not displayed—I fear the complete ritual is wanting.
translations.idiomatic: Today ascending song is performed at temple sacrifice, yet the symbolic dance is not presented—I fear the full ritual is incomplete.

sentences.zh: 夫聖王經世，異代同風，雖損益或殊，降殺迭運，未甞不執古御今，同規合矩。

translations.literal: Sage kings govern the age; different eras share the same ethos. Though additions and subtractions may differ and gradations rise and fall in turn, never have they failed to hold to antiquity to govern the present, sharing compass and square.
translations.idiomatic: Sage kings govern the age, and different eras share the same spirit. Though rites may be added to or reduced and gradations shift with the times, they have never failed to hold antiquity as guide for the present, keeping to the same measure and rule.

sentences.zh: 方茲休明在辰，文物大備，禮儀遺逸，罔不具舉，而況出祗降神，輟樂於郊祭，昭德舞功，有闕於廟享。

translations.literal: Just now in this flourishing bright era cultural achievements are fully complete and lost rites are all restored—how much more should spirits be summoned downward, yet music is suspended at suburban sacrifice, and virtue displayed and merit danced are lacking at temple feasts?
translations.idiomatic: In this flourishing age, cultural achievements are fully in place and lost rites have all been restored—how then can spirits be summoned downward while music is omitted from suburban sacrifice, and virtue displayed and merit danced be lacking from temple feasts?

sentences.zh: 謂郊廟宜設備樂。

translations.literal: I say suburban and temple rites should have complete music installed.
translations.idiomatic: I propose that suburban and temple rites should have full musical accompaniment.

sentences.zh: 」於是使內外博議。

translations.literal: " Thereupon they ordered broad deliberation inside and outside court.
translations.idiomatic: " The court then ordered broad deliberation among officials inside and outside the palace.

sentences.zh: 驃騎大將軍竟陵王誕等五十一人並同萬秋議。

translations.literal: Cavalry General in Chief, Prince of Jingling Dan, and fifty-one others all agreed with Wanqiu's proposal.
translations.idiomatic: Cavalry General in Chief, Prince of Jingling Dan, and fifty-one others all concurred with Wanqiu's proposal.

sentences.zh: 尚書左僕射建平王宏議以為：「聖王之德雖同，剏制之禮或異，樂不相沿，禮無因襲。

translations.literal: Vice Director of the Left of the Ministerial Court, Prince of Pingjian Hong, argued: "Though sage kings' virtue is the same, the rites they establish may differ—music is not transmitted unchanged, ritual has no inheriting by rote.
translations.idiomatic: Vice Director of the Left of the Ministerial Court, Prince of Pingjian Hong, argued: "Though the virtue of sage kings is the same, the rites each establishes may differ—music is not handed down unchanged, and ritual should not be inherited by rote.

sentences.zh: 自寶命開基，皇符在運，業富前王，風通振古，朝儀國章，並循先代。

translations.literal: Since the sacred mandate opened the foundation and the imperial talisman was in its course, achievements surpassed former kings, influence reached back to antiquity, and court ceremony and national statutes all followed former ages.
translations.idiomatic: Since the sacred mandate founded the dynasty and the imperial destiny was in its course, achievements surpassed those of earlier kings, influence reached back to antiquity, and court ceremony and national statutes all followed former ages.

sentences.zh: 自後晉東遷，日不暇給，雖大典略備，遺闕尚多。

translations.literal: After the Eastern migration of Jin, days allowed no respite; though great ceremonies were roughly complete, omissions remained many.
translations.idiomatic: After the Eastern Jin migration, there was no time to spare; though major ceremonies were roughly in place, many gaps remained.

sentences.zh: 至於樂號廟禮，未該往正。

translations.literal: As for music names and temple ritual, they did not accord with proper precedent.
translations.idiomatic: As for music titles and temple ritual, they no longer accorded with proper precedent.

sentences.zh: 今帝德再昌，大孝御寓，宜討定禮本，以昭來葉。

translations.literal: Now the emperor's virtue flourishes again and great filial piety holds the realm—one should investigate and fix the ritual foundation to manifest it to future generations.
translations.idiomatic: Now the emperor's virtue flourishes anew and great filial piety governs the realm—it is time to investigate and fix the ritual foundation for future generations.

sentences.zh: 尋舜樂稱《韶》，漢改《文始》，周樂《大武》，秦革《五行》。

translations.literal: Consider: Shun's music was called Shao; Han changed it to Wen Shi; Zhou's music was Grand Martial; Qin revised it to Five Elements.
translations.idiomatic: Consider: Shun's music was called Shao; Han renamed it Wen Shi; Zhou used Grand Martial; Qin replaced it with Five Elements.

sentences.zh: 眷夫祖有功而宗有德，故漢高祖廟樂稱《武德》，太宗廟樂曰《昭德》。

translations.literal: Reflect that the founder honors merit and the temple ancestor honors virtue—thus Han Gaozu's temple music was called Martial Virtue, and Taizong's temple music was called Bright Virtue.
translations.idiomatic: Since the founder honors merit and the temple ancestor honors virtue, Han Gaozu's temple music was called Martial Virtue, and Taizong's temple music was called Bright Virtue.

sentences.zh: 魏制《武始》舞武廟，制《咸熙》舞文廟。

translations.literal: Wei established Wu Shi to dance at the martial temple and Xian Xi to dance at the civil temple.
translations.idiomatic: Wei established Wu Shi for the martial temple and Xian Xi for the civil temple.

sentences.zh: 則祖宗之廟，別有樂名。

translations.literal: Thus the founder's and temple ancestor's shrines each had separate music names.
translations.idiomatic: Thus the founder's and temple ancestor's shrines each had its own music name.

sentences.zh: 晉氏之樂，《正德》《大豫》，及宋不更名，直為《前》《後》二舞，依據昔代，義舛事乖。

translations.literal: Jin's music, Zheng De and Da Yu, and Song did not rename them but simply called them the Front and Rear dances—relying on former ages in meaning and practice, both are wrong.
translations.idiomatic: Jin's Zheng De and Da Yu dances were left unchanged by Song and simply called the Front and Rear dances—following former ages in name but wrong in both principle and practice.

sentences.zh: 今宜釐改權稱，以《凱容》為《韶舞》，《宣烈》為《武舞》。

translations.literal: Now one should rectify provisional names: make Kai Rong the Shao dance and Xuan Lie the Martial dance.
