translations.idiomatic: Now provisional titles should be corrected: Kai Rong should become the Shao dance, and Xuan Lie the Martial dance.

sentences.zh: 祖宗廟樂，總以德為名。

translations.literal: Founder and temple ancestor music should all take virtue as their name.
translations.idiomatic: Music for the founder's and temple ancestor's shrines should all be named for virtue.

sentences.zh: 若廟非不毀，則樂無別稱，猶漢高、文、武，咸有嘉號，惠、景二主，樂無餘名。

translations.literal: If temples are not destroyed unless merited, then music has no separate title—as Han Gaozu, Wen, and Wu all had fine designations, while Emperors Hui and Jing had no extra music names.
translations.idiomatic: If temples are not demolished unless merited, then music needs no separate title—Han Gaozu, Wen, and Wu all had fine designations, while Emperors Hui and Jing had no additional music names.

sentences.zh: 章皇太后廟，依諸儒議，唯奏文樂。

translations.literal: At Empress Dowager Zhang's temple, following the classicists' proposal, only civil music should be played.
translations.idiomatic: At Empress Dowager Zhang's temple, following the classicists' proposal, only civil music should be performed.

sentences.zh: 何休、杜預、范寗注『初獻六羽』，並不言佾者，佾則干在其中，明婦人無武事也。

translations.literal: He Xiu, Du Yu, and Fan Ning comment on 'first offering six feathers' and none mention row-dancers; row-dancers include shields and axes among them—showing women have no martial affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He Xiu, Du Yu, and Fan Ning comment on 'first offering six feathers' and none mention row-dancers; row-dancers include shields and axes, showing that women have no martial role.

sentences.zh: 郊祀之樂，無復別名，仍同宗廟而已。

translations.literal: Suburban sacrifice music needs no separate name—it should follow the ancestral temple merely.
translations.idiomatic: Suburban sacrifice music needs no separate name and should simply follow ancestral temple practice.

sentences.zh: 尋諸《漢志》，《永至》等樂，各有義況，宜仍舊不改。

translations.literal: Searching the Han Treatise, Yong Zhi and other pieces each have their meaning and circumstances—they should remain as before, unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: Consulting the Han Treatise, Yong Zhi and other pieces each have their own meaning and context—they should remain unchanged.

sentences.zh: 宋及東晉，太祝唯送神而不迎神。

translations.literal: Under Song and Eastern Jin, the Grand Invocator only escorted the spirits out but did not welcome them in.
translations.idiomatic: Under Song and Eastern Jin, the Grand Invocator only escorted the spirits out and did not welcome them in.

sentences.zh: 近議者或云廟以居神，恒如在也，不應有迎送之事，意以為並乖其衷。

translations.literal: Recent debaters say the temple houses the spirit, always as if present—there should be no welcoming or escorting; I consider both views mistaken at heart.
translations.idiomatic: Recent debaters say the temple houses the spirit and it is always as if present, so there should be no welcoming or escorting—I consider both views to miss the point.

sentences.zh: 立廟居靈，四時致享，以申孝思之情。

translations.literal: Erecting temples to house the spirit, offering at the four seasons, is to express filial longing.
translations.idiomatic: Temples are erected to house the spirit and offerings are made through the four seasons to express filial devotion.

sentences.zh: 夫神升降無常，何必恒安所處？

translations.literal: Spirits ascend and descend without fixed rule—why must they always dwell in one place?
translations.idiomatic: Spirits ascend and descend without fixed pattern—why must they always remain in one place?

sentences.zh: 故《祭義》云：『樂以迎來，哀以送往。

translations.literal: Thus the Meaning of Sacrifice says: "Use joy to welcome arrival, use grief to escort departure.
translations.idiomatic: The Meaning of Sacrifice therefore says: "Use joy to welcome arrival and grief to escort departure.

sentences.zh: 』鄭注云：『迎來而樂，樂親之來；

translations.literal: " Zheng's commentary says: "Joy at welcoming arrival rejoices in the kin's coming;
translations.idiomatic: " Zheng's commentary explains: "Joy at welcoming arrival celebrates the kin's coming;

sentences.zh: 送往而哀，哀親之返，其享否不可知也。

translations.literal: grief at escorting departure grieves the kin's return—whether they partake is unknowable.
translations.idiomatic: grief at escorting departure mourns the kin's return—whether they have partaken is unknowable.

sentences.zh: 』《尚書》曰『祖考來格。

translations.literal: " The Documents say, "The founding ancestors come to the rite.
translations.idiomatic: " The Documents say, "The founding ancestors come to the rite.

sentences.zh: 』《詩》云：『神保遹歸。

translations.literal: " The Odes say: "The spirit-protector swiftly returns.
translations.idiomatic: " The Odes say: "The spirit-protector swiftly returns.

sentences.zh: 』注曰：『歸於天地也。

translations.literal: " The commentary says: "Returns to Heaven and Earth.
translations.idiomatic: " The commentary explains: "Returns to Heaven and Earth.

sentences.zh: 』此並言神有去來則有送迎，明矣。

translations.literal: " All these say that when spirits come and go there is escorting and welcoming—clearly.
translations.idiomatic: " All of these show that when spirits come and go there is welcoming and escorting—it is clear.

sentences.zh: 即周《肆夏》之名，備迎送之樂。

translations.literal: This is the Zhou name Si Xia, providing music for welcoming and escorting.
translations.idiomatic: This is the Zhou piece Si Xia, providing music for both welcoming and escorting.

sentences.zh: 古以尸象神，故《儀禮》祝有迎尸送尸，近代雖無尸，豈可闕迎送之禮？

translations.literal: Antiquity used the corpse to represent the spirit, so the Ceremonies have the invocator welcome and escort the corpse; though recent times have no corpse, how can welcoming and escorting be omitted?
translations.idiomatic: In antiquity the corpse represented the spirit, so the Ceremonies require the invocator to welcome and escort the corpse. Though later ages no longer use a corpse, how can the welcoming and escorting rites be omitted?

sentences.zh: 又傅玄有迎神送神歌辭，明江左不迎，非舊典也。」

translations.literal: Moreover Fu Xuan has lyrics for welcoming and escorting spirits—showing that the Eastern Court's failure to welcome is not the old canon."
translations.idiomatic: Moreover Fu Xuan composed lyrics for welcoming and escorting spirits, showing that the Eastern Court's failure to welcome spirits is not the old canon."

sentences.zh: 散騎常侍、丹陽尹建城縣開國侯顏竣議以為：「德業殊稱，則干羽異容，時無沿制，故物有損益。

translations.literal: Attendant Cavalier at Large, Administrator of Danyang, Marquis of Jiancheng Yan Jun argued: "When virtue and achievement differ in title, shields and feathers differ in form; when the times do not transmit old systems, things are added to or reduced.
translations.idiomatic: Attendant Cavalier at Large, Administrator of Danyang, Marquis of Jiancheng Yan Jun argued: "When virtue and achievement differ in title, shields and feathers differ in form; when the times do not transmit old systems, things are added to or reduced.

sentences.zh: 至於禮失道諐，稱習忘反，中興釐運，視聽所革，先代繆章，宜見刊正。

translations.literal: When ritual loses the Way and goes astray, habit becomes so ingrained one forgets to return—in this restoration and reordering, what eyes and ears must reform, the erroneous statutes of former ages should be revised.
translations.idiomatic: When ritual loses the Way and goes astray, habit becomes so ingrained that one forgets to return. In this restoration and reordering, what eyes and ears must reform includes the erroneous statutes of former ages, which should be revised.

sentences.zh: 郊之有樂，盖生《周易》《周官》，歷代著議，莫不援准。

translations.literal: Music at suburban rites arose from the Book of Changes and Rites of Zhou; dynasties recorded debates, all citing them as authority.
translations.idiomatic: Music at suburban rites originated in the Book of Changes and Rites of Zhou; dynasties recorded debates on the subject, all citing them as authority.

sentences.zh: 夫『掃地而祭，器用陶匏』，唯質與誠，以章天德，文物之備，理固不然。

translations.literal: The phrase 'sweep the ground to sacrifice, use pottery and gourds' values only simplicity and sincerity to manifest Heaven's virtue—the full array of cultural artifacts is surely not so in principle.
translations.idiomatic: The phrase 'sweep the ground to sacrifice, use pottery and gourds' values simplicity and sincerity to manifest Heaven's virtue—it does not mean that the full array of cultural artifacts is inappropriate in principle.

sentences.zh: 《周官》曰：『國有故，則旅上帝及四望。

translations.literal: The Rites of Zhou say: "When the state has an emergency, perform the itinerant rite to the Supreme Lord and the Four Outlooks.
translations.idiomatic: The Rites of Zhou state: "When the state has an emergency, perform the itinerant rite to the Supreme Lord and the Four Outlooks.

sentences.zh: 』又曰：『四圭有邸，以祀天旅上帝。

translations.literal: " Again: "Four jade tablets with bases, to sacrifice to Heaven and perform the itinerant rite to the Supreme Lord.
translations.idiomatic: " It also says: "Four jade tablets with bases, to sacrifice to Heaven and perform the itinerant rite to the Supreme Lord.

sentences.zh: 兩圭有邸，以祀地旅四望。

translations.literal: Two jade tablets with bases, to sacrifice to Earth and perform the itinerant rite to the Four Outlooks.
translations.idiomatic: Two jade tablets with bases, to sacrifice to Earth and perform the itinerant rite to the Four Outlooks.

sentences.zh: 』四望非地，則知上帝非天。

translations.literal: " The Four Outlooks are not Earth—then know the Supreme Lord is not Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: " Since the Four Outlooks are not Earth, the Supreme Lord must not be Heaven.

sentences.zh: 《孝經》云：『郊祀後稷以配天，宗祀文王於明堂，以配上帝。

translations.literal: The Classic of Filial Piety says: "Sacrifice to Hou Ji at the suburb to pair with Heaven; honor-sacrifice to King Wen in the Bright Hall to pair with the Supreme Lord.
translations.idiomatic: The Classic of Filial Piety says: "Sacrifice to Hou Ji at the suburb to pair with Heaven; honor King Wen in the Bright Hall to pair with the Supreme Lord.

sentences.zh: 』則《豫》之作樂，非郊天也。

translations.literal: " Then the Yu sacrifice's making of music is not suburban sacrifice to Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: " Therefore the music made for the Yu sacrifice is not suburban sacrifice to Heaven.

sentences.zh: 大司樂職，『奏黃鐘，歌大呂，舞《雲門》，以祀天神。

translations.literal: The Grand Master of Music's office: "Play the yellow bell, sing the great tube, dance the Cloud Gate, to sacrifice to the celestial spirits.
translations.idiomatic: The Grand Master of Music's office states: "Play the yellow bell, sing the great tube, dance the Cloud Gate, to sacrifice to the celestial spirits.

sentences.zh: 』鄭注：『天神，五帝及日月星辰也。

translations.literal: " Zheng's commentary: "Celestial spirits—the Five Emperors plus sun, moon, and stars.
translations.idiomatic: " Zheng's commentary explains: "Celestial spirits means the Five Emperors together with the sun, moon, and stars.

sentences.zh: 』王者以夏正月祀其所受命之帝於南郊，則二至之祀，又非天地。

translations.literal: " The king sacrifices at the southern suburb in the first month of summer to the emperor from whom he received the mandate—then the two solstice sacrifices are again not Heaven and Earth.
translations.idiomatic: " The king sacrifices at the southern suburb in the first month of summer to the emperor from whom he received the mandate—so the two solstice sacrifices are again not sacrifices to Heaven and Earth.

sentences.zh: 考之眾經，郊祀有樂，未見明證。

translations.literal: Examining the various classics, music at suburban sacrifice lacks clear proof.
translations.idiomatic: Examining the various classics, there is no clear proof that suburban sacrifice included music.

sentences.zh: 宗廟之禮，事炳載籍。

translations.literal: Ancestral temple ritual is clearly recorded in written sources.
translations.idiomatic: Ancestral temple ritual is clearly documented in the written sources.

sentences.zh: 爰自漢元，迄乎有晉，雖時或更制，大抵相因，為不襲名號而已。

translations.literal: From Han Yuan down to Jin, though systems sometimes changed, they largely continued—the only point was not inheriting titles.
translations.idiomatic: From Han Yuan down to Jin, though systems sometimes changed, they largely continued—the only difference was in not inheriting titles.

sentences.zh: 今樂曲淪滅，知音世希，改作之事，臣聞其語。

translations.literal: Now melodies are lost and those who know music are rare—I have heard talk of composing anew.
translations.idiomatic: Now melodies are lost and those who understand music are rare—I have heard proposals for composing anew.

sentences.zh: 《正德》《大豫》，禮容具存，宜殊其徽號，飾而用之。

translations.literal: Zheng De and Da Yu—the ritual forms fully survive; one should distinguish their insignia and adorn them for use.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng De and Da Yu—their ritual forms fully survive; their titles should be distinguished and they should be adorned for use.

sentences.zh: 以《正德》為《宣化之舞》，《大豫》為《興和之舞》，庶足以光表世烈，悅被後昆。

translations.literal: Make Zheng De the Dance of Proclaiming Transformation and Da Yu the Dance of Raising Harmony—perhaps enough to glorify the dynasty's achievements and spread joy to posterity.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng De should become the Dance of Proclaiming Transformation and Da Yu the Dance of Raising Harmony—enough, perhaps, to glorify the dynasty's achievements and spread joy to posterity.

sentences.zh: 前漢祖宗廟處各異，主名既革，舞號亦殊。

translations.literal: Former Han's founder and temple ancestor shrines stood in different places; main titles already differed, and dance names too were distinct.
translations.idiomatic: In Former Han the founder's and temple ancestor's shrines stood in different places; their main titles already differed, and their dance names were distinct as well.

sentences.zh: 今七廟合食，庭殿共所，舞蹈之容，不得廟有別制。

translations.literal: Now seven temples share combined offerings, hall and courtyard are common—the dance forms cannot have separate arrangements per temple.
translations.idiomatic: Now the seven temples share combined offerings in a common hall and courtyard—the dance forms cannot have separate arrangements for each temple.

sentences.zh: 後漢東平王蒼已議之矣。

translations.literal: Eastern Han's Prince of Dongping Cang already debated this.
translations.idiomatic: Eastern Han's Prince of Dongping Cang already debated this point.

sentences.zh: 又王肅、韓祗以王者德廣，無外六代四夷之舞、金石絲竹之樂，宜備奏宗廟。

translations.literal: Also Wang Su and Han Zhi held that when the king's virtue is broad, the dances of six dynasties and four barbarians and music of bells, stones, silk, and bamboo should all be fully performed at the ancestral temple.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Su and Han Zhi also held that when the king's virtue is broad, the dances of six dynasties and four barbarians and the music of bells, stones, silk, and bamboo should all be fully performed at the ancestral temple.

sentences.zh: 愚謂蒼、肅、祗議，合於典禮，適於當今。」

translations.literal: I deem the proposals of Cang, Su, and Zhi accord with canonical ritual and suit the present age."
translations.idiomatic: I believe the proposals of Cang, Su, and Zhi accord with canonical ritual and suit the present age."

sentences.zh: 左僕射建平王宏又議：「竣據《周禮》《孝經》，天與上帝，連文重出，故謂上帝非天，則《易》之作樂，非為祭天也。

translations.literal: Vice Director of the Left Prince of Pingjian Hong argued again: "Jun relies on the Rites of Zhou and Classic of Filial Piety—Heaven and Supreme Lord appear together in repeated phrases, so he says the Supreme Lord is not Heaven; then the Book of Changes' making music is not for sacrificing to Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Vice Director of the Left Prince of Pingjian Hong argued in reply: "Jun relies on the Rites of Zhou and Classic of Filial Piety—because Heaven and Supreme Lord appear together in repeated phrases, he concludes the Supreme Lord is not Heaven, and therefore that the Book of Changes' making of music is not for sacrificing to Heaven.

sentences.zh: 按《易》稱『先王以作樂崇德，殷薦之上帝，以配祖考。

translations.literal: Examining the Changes, it says: "The former kings made music to exalt virtue; in the Yu sacrifice they presented to the Supreme Lord, pairing with the founding ancestors.
translations.idiomatic: Examining the Changes, it says: "The former kings made music to exalt virtue; in the Yu sacrifice they presented offerings to the Supreme Lord, paired with the founding ancestors.

sentences.zh: 』《尚書》云：『肆類于上帝。

translations.literal: " The Documents say: "Perform the general sacrifice to the Supreme Lord.
translations.idiomatic: " The Documents say: "Perform the general sacrifice to the Supreme Lord.

sentences.zh: 』《春秋傳》曰：『告昊天上帝。

translations.literal: " The Spring and Autumn Commentary says: "Announce to Grand Heaven, Supreme Lord.
translations.idiomatic: " The Spring and Autumn Commentary says: "Announce to Grand Heaven, Supreme Lord.

sentences.zh: 』凡上帝之言，無非天也。

translations.literal: " Every mention of Supreme Lord is none other than Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: " Every reference to the Supreme Lord is none other than Heaven.

sentences.zh: 天尊不可以一稱，故或謂昊天，或謂上帝，或謂昊天上帝，不得以天有數稱，便謂上帝非天。

translations.literal: Heaven's exaltation cannot be limited to one title—thus sometimes it is called Grand Heaven, sometimes Supreme Lord, sometimes Grand Heaven Supreme Lord; one cannot because Heaven has several titles conclude Supreme Lord is not Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven's exaltation cannot be limited to a single title—thus it is sometimes called Grand Heaven, sometimes Supreme Lord, sometimes Grand Heaven Supreme Lord. One cannot because Heaven has several titles conclude that the Supreme Lord is not Heaven.

sentences.zh: 徐邈推《周禮》『國有故，則旅上帝』，以知禮天，旅上帝，同是祭天。

translations.literal: Xu Miao inferred from the Rites of Zhou 'when the state has an emergency, perform the itinerant rite to the Supreme Lord' to know that ritual to Heaven and itinerant rite to Supreme Lord are both sacrificing to Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Miao inferred from the Rites of Zhou's 'when the state has an emergency, perform the itinerant rite to the Supreme Lord' that ritual to Heaven and the itinerant rite to the Supreme Lord are both sacrifices to Heaven.

sentences.zh: 言禮天者，謂常祀也；

translations.literal: Speaking of ritual to Heaven means the regular sacrifice;
translations.idiomatic: Speaking of ritual to Heaven refers to the regular sacrifice;

sentences.zh: 旅上帝者，有故而祭也。

translations.literal: itinerant rite to Supreme Lord means sacrifice when there is cause.
translations.idiomatic: the itinerant rite to the Supreme Lord refers to sacrifice when there is special cause.

sentences.zh: 《孝經》稱『嚴父莫大於配天』，故云『郊祀後稷以配天，宗祀文王於明堂，以配上帝。

translations.literal: The Classic of Filial Piety says 'honoring the father—nothing greater than pairing with Heaven,' thus 'sacrifice to Hou Ji at the suburb to pair with Heaven; honor-sacrifice to King Wen in the Bright Hall to pair with the Supreme Lord.
translations.idiomatic: The Classic of Filial Piety says 'honoring the father—nothing greater than pairing with Heaven,' and therefore states 'sacrifice to Hou Ji at the suburb to pair with Heaven; honor King Wen in the Bright Hall to pair with the Supreme Lord.

sentences.zh: 』既天為議，則上帝猶天益明也。

translations.literal: " Since Heaven is the topic of debate, Supreme Lord as Heaven is all the clearer.
translations.idiomatic: " Since Heaven is the topic under discussion, the Supreme Lord as Heaven is all the clearer.

sentences.zh: 不欲使二天文同，故變上帝爾。

translations.literal: One does not wish two sentences on Heaven to read identically—thus the change to Supreme Lord.
translations.idiomatic: The text does not wish two sentences on Heaven to read identically—hence the shift to Supreme Lord.

sentences.zh: 《周禮》祀天之言再見，故鄭注以前天神為五帝，後冬至所祭為昊天。

translations.literal: The Rites of Zhou mention sacrificing to Heaven twice—thus Zheng's commentary takes the earlier celestial spirits as the Five Emperors and the later winter-solstice sacrifice as Grand Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: The Rites of Zhou mention sacrificing to Heaven twice—thus Zheng's commentary takes the earlier celestial spirits as the Five Emperors and the later winter-solstice sacrifice as Grand Heaven.

sentences.zh: 竣又云『二至之祀，又非天地。

translations.literal: Jun also says 'the two solstice sacrifices are again not Heaven and Earth.
translations.idiomatic: Jun also argues that 'the two solstice sacrifices are again not sacrifices to Heaven and Earth.

sentences.zh: 』未知天地竟應以何時致享？

translations.literal: " One does not know when Heaven and Earth should actually receive sacrifice?
translations.idiomatic: " But when, then, should Heaven and Earth actually receive sacrifice?

sentences.zh: 《記》云：『掃地而祭，器用陶匏。

translations.literal: The Record says: "Sweep the ground to sacrifice, use pottery and gourds.
translations.idiomatic: The Record says: "Sweep the ground to sacrifice, use pottery and gourds.

sentences.zh: 』旨明所用質素，無害以樂降神。

translations.literal: " Its point is that what is used is plain and simple—it does not forbid using music to summon spirits downward.
translations.idiomatic: " Its point is that what is used should be plain and simple—it does not forbid using music to summon the spirits downward.

sentences.zh: 萬秋謂郊宜有樂，事有典據。

translations.literal: Wanqiu says the suburb should have music—there is canonical basis for this.
translations.idiomatic: Wanqiu's view that suburban sacrifice should include music has canonical support.

sentences.zh: 竣又云『東平王蒼以為前漢諸祖別廟，是以祖宗之廟可得各有舞樂。

translations.literal: Jun also says 'Prince of Dongping Cang held that former Han's various ancestors had separate temples—thus founder and temple ancestor shrines could each have their own dance music.
translations.idiomatic: Jun also notes that 'Prince of Dongping Cang held that Former Han's various ancestors had separate temples, and therefore founder and temple ancestor shrines could each have their own dance music.

sentences.zh: 至於祫祭始祖之廟，則專用始祖之舞。

translations.literal: As for the joint sacrifice at the founding ancestor's temple, only the founding ancestor's dance was used.
translations.idiomatic: At the joint sacrifice in the founding ancestor's temple, only the founding ancestor's dance was used.

sentences.zh: 故謂後漢諸祖，共廟同庭，雖有祖宗，不宜入別舞。

translations.literal: Thus he holds that later Han's various ancestors shared temples and one courtyard—though there were founder and temple ancestors, separate dances should not be introduced.
translations.idiomatic: He therefore holds that Later Han's various ancestors shared temples and one courtyard, and that although there were founder and temple ancestors, separate dances should not be introduced.

sentences.zh: 』此誠一家之意，而未統適時之變也。

translations.literal: " This is indeed one school's opinion, but it has not grasped changes suited to the times.
translations.idiomatic: " This is indeed one school's opinion, but it fails to account for changes suited to the times.

sentences.zh: 後漢從儉，故諸祖共廟，猶以異室存別室之禮。

translations.literal: Later Han practiced frugality, so various ancestors shared temples, yet with separate chambers preserved the ritual of distinct rooms.
translations.idiomatic: Later Han practiced frugality, so various ancestors shared temples, yet separate chambers preserved the ritual of distinct rooms.

sentences.zh: 晉氏以來，登歌誦美，諸室繼作。

translations.literal: Since the Jin house, ascending song chanted praise, and each chamber performed in succession.
translations.idiomatic: Since the Jin dynasty, ascending song has chanted praise, with each chamber performing in succession.

sentences.zh: 至於祖宗樂舞，何獨不可迭奏。

translations.literal: As for founder and temple ancestor music and dance, why alone may they not be performed in succession?
translations.idiomatic: As for the music and dances of the founder and temple ancestors, why should they alone not be performed in succession?

sentences.zh: 苟所詠者殊，雖復共庭，亦非嫌也。

translations.literal: If what is chanted differs, though they share one courtyard, there is no objection.
translations.idiomatic: If what is sung differs, there is no objection even when they share the same courtyard.

sentences.zh: 魏三祖各有舞樂，豈復是異廟邪？

translations.literal: Wei's three founding emperors each had their own dance music—were they in separate temples?
translations.idiomatic: Wei's three founding emperors each had distinct dance music—surely they were not in separate temples?

sentences.zh: 」眾議並同宏：「祠南郊迎神，奏《肆夏》。

translations.literal: " The assembled deliberations all agreed with Hong: "At sacrifice at the southern suburb, to welcome the spirits, play Si Xia.
translations.idiomatic: " The assembled deliberations all agreed with Hong: "At the southern suburban sacrifice, to welcome the spirits, play Si Xia.

sentences.zh: 初登壇，奏登歌。

translations.literal: On first ascending the altar, play ascending song.
translations.idiomatic: On first ascending the altar, perform ascending song.

sentences.zh: 初獻，奏《凱容》《宣烈》之舞。

translations.literal: At the first offering, perform the Kai Rong and Xuan Lie dances.
translations.idiomatic: At the first offering, perform the Kai Rong and Xuan Lie dances.

sentences.zh: 送神，奏《肆夏》。

translations.literal: In escorting the spirits, play Si Xia.
translations.idiomatic: In escorting the spirits out, play Si Xia.

sentences.zh: 祠廟迎神，奏《肆夏》。

translations.literal: At temple sacrifice to welcome the spirits, play Si Xia.
translations.idiomatic: At temple sacrifice, to welcome the spirits, play Si Xia.

sentences.zh: 皇帝入廟門，奏《永至》。

translations.literal: When the emperor enters the temple gate, play Everlasting Arrival.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor enters the temple gate, play Everlasting Arrival.

sentences.zh: 皇帝詣東壁，奏登歌。

translations.literal: When the emperor proceeds to the eastern wall, play ascending song.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor proceeds to the eastern wall, perform ascending song.

sentences.zh: 初獻，奏《凱容》《宣烈》之舞。

translations.literal: At the first offering, perform the Kai Rong and Xuan Lie dances.
translations.idiomatic: At the first offering, perform the Kai Rong and Xuan Lie dances.

sentences.zh: 終獻，奏《永安》。

translations.literal: At the final offering, play Everlasting Peace.
translations.idiomatic: At the final offering, play Everlasting Peace.

sentences.zh: 送神，奏《肆夏》。

translations.literal: In escorting the spirits, play Si Xia.
translations.idiomatic: In escorting the spirits out, play Si Xia.

sentences.zh: 」詔可。

translations.literal: " The edict approved.
translations.idiomatic: " The edict approved.

sentences.zh: 孝建二年十月辛未，有司又奏：「郊廟舞樂，皇帝親奉，初登壇及入廟詣東壁，並奏登歌，不及三公行事。

translations.literal: On the xinwei day of the tenth month of the second year of Xiaojian, the relevant offices memorialized again: "For suburban and temple dance music, when the emperor personally performs the rite, on first ascending the altar and on entering the temple and proceeding to the eastern wall, ascending song is played throughout—it does not extend to when the Three Excellencies perform the rite.
translations.idiomatic: On the xinwei day of the tenth month in the second year of Xiaojian, the relevant offices memorialized again: "For suburban and temple dance music, when the emperor personally performs the rite, ascending song is played on first ascending the altar and on entering the temple and proceeding to the eastern wall—but not when the Three Excellencies perform the rite.

sentences.zh: 」左僕射建平王宏重參議：「公卿行事，亦宜奏登歌。

translations.literal: " Vice Director of the Left Prince of Pingjian Hong deliberated again: "When the high ministers perform the rite, ascending song should also be played.
translations.idiomatic: " Vice Director of the Left Prince of Pingjian Hong deliberated further: "When the high ministers perform the rite, ascending song should also be performed.

sentences.zh: 」有司又奏：「元會及二廟齊祠，登歌伎舊並於殿庭設作。

translations.literal: " The relevant offices memorialized again: "At the New Year's assembly and joint sacrifice at the two temples, ascending song performers were formerly set up in the hall courtyard.
translations.idiomatic: " The relevant offices memorialized again: "At the New Year's assembly and joint sacrifice at the two temples, ascending song performers were formerly stationed in the hall courtyard.

sentences.zh: 尋廟祠，依新儀注，登歌人上殿，弦管在下；

translations.literal: Examining temple sacrifice, according to the new ritual notes, ascending song performers go up to the hall and strings and pipes are below;
translations.idiomatic: Reviewing temple sacrifice, under the new ritual instructions ascending song performers go up to the hall while strings and pipes remain below;

sentences.zh: 今元會，登歌人亦上殿，弦管在下。

translations.literal: now at the New Year's assembly, ascending song performers also go up to the hall, strings and pipes below.
translations.idiomatic: now at the New Year's assembly, ascending song performers also go up to the hall, with strings and pipes below.

sentences.zh: 」並詔可。

translations.literal: " Both were approved by edict.
translations.idiomatic: " Both proposals were approved by edict.

sentences.zh: 文帝章太后廟未有樂章，孝武大明中使尚書左丞殷淡造新歌，明帝又自造昭太后宣太后歌詩。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen's Empress Dowager Zhang temple had no music sections; in Daming under Emperor Xiaowu he had Left Assistant Director of the Ministerial Court Yin Dan compose new songs; Emperor Ming personally composed songs for Empress Dowager Zhao and Empress Dowager Xuan.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen's Empress Dowager Zhang temple had no musical sections. In the Daming era under Emperor Xiaowu, Left Assistant Director Yin Dan was ordered to compose new songs; Emperor Ming personally composed songs for Empress Dowagers Zhao and Xuan.

sentences.zh: 後漢正月旦，天子臨德陽殿受朝賀，舍利從西方來，戲於殿前，激水化成比目魚，跳躍嗽水，作霧翳日；

translations.literal: On New Year's Day in Later Han, the Son of Heaven attended at Deyang Hall to receive court congratulations; a shari came from the west and performed before the hall, spraying water that transformed into flatfish leaping and spouting water, making mist that shaded the sun;
translations.idiomatic: On New Year's Day in Later Han, the Son of Heaven attended Deyang Hall to receive court congratulations. A shari came from the west and performed before the hall, spraying water that transformed into flatfish leaping and spouting, making mist that shaded the sun;

sentences.zh: 畢，又化成黃龍，長八九丈，出水游戲，炫燿日光。

translations.literal: when finished, it transformed again into a yellow dragon eight or nine zhang long, emerging from the water to sport, dazzling in the sunlight.
translations.idiomatic: When finished, it transformed again into a yellow dragon eight or nine zhang long, emerging from the water to sport and dazzling in the sunlight.

sentences.zh: 以兩大絲繩繫兩柱頭，相去數丈，兩倡女對舞，行於繩上，相逢切肩而不傾。

translations.literal: Two great silk ropes were tied to two pillar tops, several zhang apart; two singing girls danced facing each other, walking on the rope, meeting shoulder to shoulder without tipping.
translations.idiomatic: Two great silk ropes were tied to pillar tops several zhang apart; two singing girls danced facing each other on the rope, meeting shoulder to shoulder without tipping.

sentences.zh: 魏晉訖江左，猶有《夏育扛鼎》《巨象行乳》《神龜抃舞》《背負靈岳》《桂樹白雪》《畫地成川》之樂焉。

translations.literal: From Wei and Jin down to the Eastern Court, there still were performances such as Xia Yu Carrying the Ding, Great Elephant Giving Milk, Divine Tortoise Clapping Dance, Bearing Spirit Mountains on the Back, Cassia Tree White Snow, and Drawing Earth to Make a River.
translations.idiomatic: From Wei and Jin down to the Eastern Court, performances such as Xia Yu Carrying the Ding, Great Elephant Giving Milk, Divine Tortoise Clapping Dance, Bearing Spirit Mountains on the Back, Cassia Tree White Snow, and Drawing Earth to Make a River still survived.

sentences.zh: 晉成帝咸康七年，散騎侍郎顧臻表曰：「臣聞聖王制樂，賛揚治道，養以仁義，防其邪淫，上享宗廟，下訓黎民，體五行之正音，協八風以陶氣。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Xiankang under Emperor Cheng of Jin, Attendant Cavalier Gu Zhen submitted: "I have heard that sage kings establish music to praise the way of governance, nurture with benevolence and righteousness, guard against licentious evil, serve the ancestral temple above and instruct the people below, embody the correct tones of the Five Phases, and harmonize the eight winds to cultivate qi.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year of Xiankang under Emperor Cheng of Jin, Attendant Cavalier Gu Zhen submitted a memorial: "I have heard that sage kings establish music to praise the way of governance, nurture with benevolence and righteousness, guard against licentious evil, serve the ancestral temple above and instruct the people below, embody the correct tones of the Five Phases, and harmonize the eight winds to cultivate the spirit.

sentences.zh: 以宮聲正方而好義，角聲堅齊而率禮，弦歌鐘鼓金石之作備矣。

translations.literal: The gong tone is square and upright and loves righteousness; the jue tone is firm and orderly and leads ritual—the works of string song, bells, drums, and metal and stone are complete.
translations.idiomatic: The gong tone is square and upright and loves righteousness; the jue tone is firm and orderly and leads ritual—string songs, bells, drums, and metal and stone instruments are all in place.

sentences.zh: 故通神至化，有率舞之感；

translations.literal: Thus communicating with spirits and reaching transformation, there is the feeling of following dance;
translations.idiomatic: Thus in communicating with spirits and reaching full transformation, there is the feeling of spontaneous following dance;

sentences.zh: 移風改俗，致和樂之極。

translations.literal: transforming customs and changing habits, reaching the utmost of harmony and joy.
translations.idiomatic: transforming customs and changing habits to reach the utmost harmony and joy.

sentences.zh: 末世之伎，設禮外之觀，逆行連倒，頭足入筥之屬，皮肩外剝，肝心內摧。

translations.literal: Performances of decadent ages set spectacles outside ritual—walking inverted and tumbling head over heels, putting head and feet into baskets, flaying skin from shoulders, crushing liver and heart within.
translations.idiomatic: Performances of decadent ages set spectacles outside ritual—walking inverted and tumbling head over heels, putting head and feet into baskets, flaying skin from shoulders, crushing liver and heart within.

sentences.zh: 敦彼行葦，猶謂勿踐，矧伊生民，而不惻愴。

translations.literal: Thick are those reeds by the road—still one says do not trample them; how much more living people—should one not feel compassion?
translations.idiomatic: Thick are those reeds by the road—still we are told not to trample them; how much more should we feel compassion for living people?

sentences.zh: 加以四海朝覲，言觀帝庭，耳聆《雅》《頌》之聲，目覩威儀之序，足以蹋天，頭以履地，反兩儀之順，傷彝倫之大。

translations.literal: Moreover the four seas come to court, saying they observe the imperial court—yet ears hear not the sounds of the Odes and Hymns, eyes see not the order of dignified ceremony; enough to tread on Heaven and walk on earth with one's head, reversing the order of the Two Principles and harming the great human bonds.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover the four seas come to court expecting to observe the imperial court—yet their ears hear not the sounds of the Odes and Hymns, their eyes see not dignified ceremony; it is as if feet tread on Heaven and heads walk on earth, reversing the order of the Two Principles and violating the great human bonds.

sentences.zh: 方今夷狄對岸，外御為急，兵食七升，忘身赴難，過泰之戲，日稟五斗。

translations.literal: Just now barbarians face us across the river and external defense is urgent—soldiers live on seven sheng of grain and forget themselves in hardship, while excessive entertainments receive five dou per day.
translations.idiomatic: Just now barbarians face us across the river and external defense is urgent—soldiers subsist on seven sheng of grain and risk their lives in hardship, while excessive entertainments receive five dou per day.

sentences.zh: 方埽神州，經略中甸，若此之事，不可示遠。

translations.literal: Just as we sweep clean the divine land and strategize the central realm, such things cannot be shown to distant peoples.
translations.idiomatic: Just as we sweep clean the divine land and strategize the central realm, such things must not be displayed to distant peoples.

sentences.zh: 宜下太常，纂備雅樂，《簫韶》九成，惟新於盛運；

translations.literal: The Grand Master of Ceremonies should be ordered to compile and prepare elegant music—the nine movements of Xiao Shao, renewed for this flourishing age;
translations.idiomatic: The Grand Master of Ceremonies should be ordered to compile and prepare elegant music—the nine movements of Xiao Shao, renewed for this flourishing age;

sentences.zh: 功德頌聲，永著于來茲。

translations.literal: hymns of merit and virtue, forever recorded for generations to come.
translations.idiomatic: hymns of merit and virtue, forever recorded for generations to come.

sentences.zh: 此乃《詩》所以『燕及皇天，克昌厥後』者也。

translations.literal: This is what the Odes mean by 'feasting and reaching Grand Heaven, making posterity flourish.'
translations.idiomatic: This is what the Odes mean by 'feasting and reaching Grand Heaven, making posterity flourish.'

sentences.zh: 雜伎而傷人者，皆宜除之。

translations.literal: Mixed acrobatics that harm people should all be abolished.
translations.idiomatic: Mixed acrobatics that harm people should all be abolished.

sentences.zh: 流簡儉之德，邁康哉之詠，清風既行，民應如草，此之謂也。

translations.literal: Spread the virtue of simplicity and frugality, surpass the hymn 'How Grand'—when the clear wind blows, the people respond like grass; this is what is meant.
translations.idiomatic: Spread the virtue of simplicity and frugality, surpass the hymn 'How Grand'—when the clear wind blows, the people respond like grass; this is what is meant.

sentences.zh: 愚管之誠，惟垂采察。

translations.literal: This humble opinion I offer—may Your Majesty graciously examine it.
translations.idiomatic: This humble opinion I offer—may Your Majesty graciously examine it.

sentences.zh: 」於是除《高絙》《紫鹿》《跂行》《鱉食》及《齊王捲衣》《笮兒》等樂。

translations.literal: " Thereupon High Rope, Purple Deer, Handwalking, Turtle Eating, and Prince of Qi Rolling Clothes, Zha Child, and other performances were abolished.
translations.idiomatic: " Thereupon High Rope, Purple Deer, Handwalking, Turtle Eating, Prince of Qi Rolling Clothes, Zha Child, and other such performances were abolished.

sentences.zh: 又減其稟。

translations.literal: Their grain rations were also reduced.
translations.idiomatic: Their grain rations were also reduced.

sentences.zh: 其後復《高絙》《紫鹿》焉。

translations.literal: Later High Rope and Purple Deer were restored.
translations.idiomatic: Later High Rope and Purple Deer were restored.

sentences.zh: 宋文帝元嘉十三年，司徒彭城王義康於東府正會，依舊給伎。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year of Yuanjia under Emperor Wen of Song, Grand Steward Prince of Pengcheng Yikang held the formal assembly at the Eastern Residence and performers were supplied as before.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year of Yuanjia under Emperor Wen of Song, Grand Steward Prince of Pengcheng Yikang held the formal assembly at the Eastern Residence, and performers were supplied as before.

sentences.zh: 總章工馮大列：「相承給諸王伎十四種，其舞伎三十六人。

translations.literal: Zongzhang artisan Feng Dalie: "By tradition princes are supplied fourteen kinds of performers; dance performers number thirty-six.
translations.idiomatic: Zongzhang artisan Feng Dalie reported: "By tradition princes are supplied fourteen kinds of performers; dance performers number thirty-six.

sentences.zh: 」太常傅隆以為：「未詳此人數所由。

translations.literal: " Grand Master of Ceremonies Fu Long held: "The origin of this number is unclear.
translations.idiomatic: " Grand Master of Ceremonies Fu Long argued: "The origin of this number is unclear.

sentences.zh: 唯杜預注《左傳》佾舞云諸侯六六三十六人，常以為非。

translations.literal: Only Du Yu's commentary on the Zuo Commentary on row-dance says feudal lords use six-six, thirty-six people—I have always considered this wrong.
translations.idiomatic: Only Du Yu's commentary on the Zuo Commentary on row-dance says feudal lords use six-six, thirty-six people—I have always considered this incorrect.

sentences.zh: 夫舞者，所以節八音者也。

translations.literal: Dancers are what regulate the eight sounds.
translations.idiomatic: Dancers are what regulate the eight sounds.

sentences.zh: 八音克諧，然後成樂。

translations.literal: When the eight sounds are harmonized, then music is complete.
translations.idiomatic: Only when the eight sounds are harmonized does music become complete.

sentences.zh: 故必以八八為列，自天子至士，降殺以兩，兩者，減其二列爾。

translations.literal: Therefore rows must be eight-by-eight; from Son of Heaven down to gentleman, gradation decreases by twos—'by twos' means reducing two rows.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore rows must be eight-by-eight; from Son of Heaven down to gentleman, gradation decreases by twos—'by twos' means reducing two rows.

sentences.zh: 預以為一列又減二人，至士止餘四人，豈復成樂。

translations.literal: Yu held that each row further reduces by two people—down to gentlemen only four remain; how could that still make music?
translations.idiomatic: Yu held that each row further reduces by two people—down to gentlemen only four remain; how could that still constitute music?

sentences.zh: 按服虔注《傳》云：『天子八八，諸侯六八，大夫四八，士二八。

translations.literal: Examining Fu Qian's commentary on the Commentary: "Son of Heaven eight-eight, feudal lords six-eight, grand officers four-eight, gentlemen two-eight.
translations.idiomatic: Examining Fu Qian's commentary on the Commentary: "Son of Heaven eight-eight, feudal lords six-eight, grand officers four-eight, gentlemen two-eight.

sentences.zh: 』其義甚允。

translations.literal: " Its meaning is very fitting.
translations.idiomatic: " Its meaning is very fitting.

sentences.zh: 今諸王不復舞佾，其總章舞伎，即古之女樂也。

translations.literal: Now princes no longer dance row-dances; their Zongzhang dance performers are the ancient women's music.
translations.idiomatic: Now princes no longer perform row-dances; their Zongzhang dance performers are the ancient women's music.

sentences.zh: 殿庭八八，諸王則應六八，理例坦然。

translations.literal: The hall courtyard uses eight-eight; princes should use six-eight—the principle is plainly clear.
translations.idiomatic: The hall courtyard uses eight-eight; princes should use six-eight—the principle is plainly clear.

sentences.zh: 又《春秋》，鄭伯納晉悼公女樂二八，晉以一八賜魏綘，此樂以八人為列之證也。

translations.literal: Also in the Spring and Autumn Annals, the Earl of Zheng presented Duke Dao of Jin female musicians two-eight; Jin gave one-eight to Wei Jiang—this is proof that music uses eight people per row.
translations.idiomatic: Also in the Spring and Autumn Annals, the Earl of Zheng presented Duke Dao of Jin female musicians two-eight; Jin gave one-eight to Wei Jiang—this proves that music uses eight people per row.

sentences.zh: 若如議者，唯天子八，則鄭應納晉二六，晉應賜綘一六也。

translations.literal: If as the debaters hold only the Son of Heaven uses eight, then Zheng should have presented Jin two-six, and Jin should have given Jiang one-six.
translations.idiomatic: If as the debaters hold only the Son of Heaven uses eight per row, then Zheng should have presented Jin two-six, and Jin should have given Jiang one-six.

sentences.zh: 自天子至士，其文物典章，尊卑差級，莫不以兩，未有諸侯既降二列，又列輙減二人，近降太半，非唯八音不具，於兩義亦乖，杜氏之謬可見矣。

translations.literal: From Son of Heaven to gentleman, cultural artifacts and statutes, high and low gradations—all decrease by twos; never have feudal lords both reduced two rows and then each row reduced by two people, nearly cutting by more than half—not only are the eight sounds incomplete, but the principle of twos is also violated; Du's error is visible.
translations.idiomatic: From Son of Heaven to gentleman, cultural artifacts and statutes, high and low gradations—all decrease by twos. Never have feudal lords both reduced two rows and then each row reduced by two people, nearly cutting by more than half—not only are the eight sounds incomplete, but the principle of twos is also violated; Du's error is evident.

sentences.zh: 國典事大，宜令詳正。

translations.literal: National statutes are weighty matters—they should be ordered investigated and corrected.
translations.idiomatic: National statutes are weighty matters—they should be investigated and corrected.

sentences.zh: 」事不施行。

translations.literal: " The proposal was not implemented.
translations.idiomatic: " The proposal was not implemented.

sentences.zh: 民之生，莫有知其始也。

translations.literal: The birth of the people—none know its beginning.
translations.idiomatic: The birth of the people—no one knows its beginning.

sentences.zh: 含靈抱智，以生天地之間。

translations.literal: Embodying spirit and holding intelligence, they are born between Heaven and Earth.
translations.idiomatic: Embodying spirit and holding intelligence, they are born between Heaven and Earth.

sentences.zh: 夫喜怒哀樂之情，好得惡失之性，不學而能，不知所以然而然者也。

translations.literal: The feelings of joy, anger, grief, and delight, the nature of loving gain and hating loss—without learning one can do them, not knowing why yet so it is.
translations.idiomatic: The feelings of joy, anger, grief, and delight, the nature of loving gain and hating loss—these come without learning; one does not know why, yet so they are.

sentences.zh: 怒則爭鬪，喜則詠歌。

translations.literal: Angry, one fights; joyful, one chants song.
translations.idiomatic: When angry, one fights; when joyful, one sings.

sentences.zh: 夫歌者，固樂之始也。

translations.literal: Song is indeed the beginning of music.
translations.idiomatic: Song is indeed the beginning of music.

sentences.zh: 詠歌不足，乃手之舞之，足之蹈之，然則舞又歌之次也。

translations.literal: When chanting song is not enough, one moves the hands in dance and the feet in stepping—thus dance is again the next after song.
translations.idiomatic: When chanting song is not enough, one moves the hands in dance and the feet in stepping—thus dance follows song.

sentences.zh: 詠歌舞蹈，所以宣其喜心，喜而無節，則流淫莫反。

translations.literal: Chanting song and dancing are to express the joyful heart; joy without measure then flows into licentiousness with no return.
translations.idiomatic: Chanting song and dancing express the joyful heart; joy without measure flows into licentiousness with no return.

sentences.zh: 故聖人以五聲和其性，以八音節其流，而故謂之樂能移風易俗，平心正體焉。

translations.literal: Therefore the sage harmonizes their nature with the five tones and regulates its flow with the eight sounds—thus it is said music can transform customs and change habits, settle the heart and correct the body.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore the sage harmonizes human nature with the five tones and regulates its flow with the eight sounds—thus it is said that music can transform customs, change habits, settle the heart, and correct the body.

sentences.zh: 昔有娥氏有二女，居九成之臺。

translations.literal: In antiquity the E clan had two daughters who lived on the Terrace of Nine Completes.
translations.idiomatic: In antiquity the E clan had two daughters who lived on the Terrace of Nine Completes.

sentences.zh: 天帝使䴏夜往，二女覆以玉筐，既而發視之，䴏遺二卵，五色，北飛不反。

translations.literal: The Celestial Emperor sent the dark swallow by night; the two daughters covered it with a jade basket, then opened it to look—the swallow left two eggs, five-colored; it flew north and did not return.
translations.idiomatic: The Celestial Emperor sent the dark swallow by night. The two daughters covered it with a jade basket, then opened it to look—the swallow had left two five-colored eggs and flew north, never to return.

sentences.zh: 二女作歌，始為北音。

translations.literal: The two daughters composed a song—this was the beginning of northern music.
translations.idiomatic: The two daughters composed a song—this was the origin of northern music.

sentences.zh: 禹省南土，嵞山之女令其妾候禹於嵞山之陽，女乃作歌，始為南音。

translations.literal: Yu inspected the southern lands; a woman of Mount Tu had her concubine wait for Yu on the southern slope of Mount Tu—the woman composed a song, the beginning of southern music.
translations.idiomatic: When Yu inspected the southern lands, a woman of Mount Tu had her attendant wait for Yu on the mountain's southern slope. The woman composed a song—the origin of southern music.

sentences.zh: 夏后孔甲田於東陽萯山，天大風晦冥，迷入民室。

translations.literal: Xia ruler Kong Jia was hunting at Mount Fu in Dongyang; great wind arose and the sky darkened, and he lost his way into a commoner's house.
translations.idiomatic: Xia ruler Kong Jia was hunting at Mount Fu in Dongyang when a great wind arose and the sky darkened. He lost his way and entered a commoner's house.

sentences.zh: 主人方乳，或曰：「后來是良日也，必大吉。

translations.literal: The master was just nursing a child; someone said: "The queen's coming on this auspicious day will surely bring great fortune.
translations.idiomatic: The master was just nursing a child when someone said: "The queen's arrival on this auspicious day will surely bring great fortune.

sentences.zh: 」或曰：「不勝之子，必有殃。

translations.literal: " Another said: "A child the household cannot support will surely bring disaster.
translations.idiomatic: " Another said: "A child the household cannot support will surely bring disaster.

sentences.zh: 」后乃取以歸，曰：「以為余子，誰敢殃之？

translations.literal: " The queen took the child and returned, saying: "I will make him my son—who would dare bring disaster upon him?
translations.idiomatic: " The queen took the child and returned, saying: "I will make him my son—who would dare bring disaster upon him?

sentences.zh: 」後析橑，斧破斷其足。

translations.literal: " Later when splitting rafters, an axe broke and cut off his foot.
translations.idiomatic: " Later, while splitting rafters, an axe broke and cut off his foot.

sentences.zh: 孔甲曰：「鳴呼！

translations.literal: Kong Jia said: "Alas!
translations.idiomatic: Kong Jia said: "Alas!

sentences.zh: 有命矣。

translations.literal: It was fated.
translations.idiomatic: It was fated.

sentences.zh: 」乃作《破斧》之歌，始為東音。

translations.literal: " He then composed the song Broken Axe—the beginning of eastern music.
translations.idiomatic: " He then composed the song Broken Axe—the origin of eastern music.

sentences.zh: 周昭王南征，殞於漢中。

translations.literal: King Zhao of Zhou marched south and perished in Hanzhong.
translations.idiomatic: King Zhao of Zhou marched south and perished in Hanzhong.

sentences.zh: 王右辛餘靡長且多力，振王北濟，周公乃封之西翟，徙宅西河，追思故處作歌，始為西音。

translations.literal: The king's attendant Xin Yumi was tall and very strong; he lifted the king and crossed north. The Duke of Zhou enfeoffed him in Western Di, moved his residence to Western River, and longing for his old place composed a song—the beginning of western music.
translations.idiomatic: The king's attendant Xin Yumi was tall and very strong; he lifted the king and crossed north. The Duke of Zhou enfeoffed him in Western Di and moved his residence to Western River. Longing for his old home, he composed a song—the origin of western music.

sentences.zh: 此蓋四方之歌也。

translations.literal: These were roughly the songs of the four directions.
translations.idiomatic: These were roughly the songs of the four directions.

sentences.zh: 黃帝、帝堯之世，王化下洽，民樂無事，故因擊壤之歡，慶雲之瑞，民因以作歌。

translations.literal: In the ages of the Yellow Emperor and Emperor Yao, royal transformation spread below and the people rejoiced in peace—thus from the joy of pounding earth and the auspiciousness of celebratory clouds, the people accordingly composed songs.
translations.idiomatic: In the ages of the Yellow Emperor and Emperor Yao, royal transformation spread throughout the realm and the people rejoiced in peace. From the joy of pounding earth and the auspiciousness of celebratory clouds, the people composed songs.

sentences.zh: 其後《風》衰《雅》缺，而妖淫靡漫之聲起。

translations.literal: Afterward the Airs declined and the Hymns were wanting, and seductive, licentious, and dissolute sounds arose.
translations.idiomatic: Afterward the Airs declined and the Hymns were wanting, and seductive, licentious, and dissolute sounds arose.

sentences.zh: 周衰，有秦青者，善謳，而薛談學謳於秦青，未窮青之伎而辭歸。

translations.literal: When Zhou declined, there was Qin Qing, skilled in song; Xue Tan studied song from Qin Qing, but before mastering Qing's art he took leave to return home.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhou declined, there was Qin Qing, skilled in song. Xue Tan studied song from Qin Qing but left for home before mastering his art.

sentences.zh: 青餞之於郊，乃撫節悲歌，聲震林木，響遏行雲。

translations.literal: Qing saw him off in the suburbs and, striking the beat, sang a mournful song—his voice shook the forest trees and halted the passing clouds.
translations.idiomatic: Qing saw him off in the suburbs and, striking the beat, sang a mournful song—his voice shook the forest trees and halted the passing clouds.

sentences.zh: 薛談遂留不去，以卒其業。

translations.literal: Xue Tan then stayed and did not leave, completing his training.
translations.idiomatic: Xue Tan then stayed and did not leave, completing his training.

sentences.zh: 又有韓娥者，東之齊，至雝門匱糧，乃鬻歌假食。

translations.literal: There was also Han E, who went east to Qi; reaching Yong Gate her provisions ran out, so she sold song to borrow food.
translations.idiomatic: There was also Han E, who went east to Qi. Reaching Yong Gate her provisions ran out, so she sold her songs to borrow food.

sentences.zh: 既而去，餘響繞梁，三日不絕。

translations.literal: When she had gone, her lingering sound circled the beams for three days without ceasing.
translations.idiomatic: When she had gone, her lingering sound circled the beams for three days without ceasing.

sentences.zh: 左右謂其人不去也。

translations.literal: Those beside her thought the person had not left.
translations.idiomatic: Those beside her thought she had not left.

sentences.zh: 過逆旅，逆旅人辱之，韓娥因曼聲哀哭，一里老幼，悲愁垂涕相對，三日不食。

translations.literal: Passing an inn, the innkeeper insulted her; Han E therefore sang a drawn-out mournful cry, and for a li around, old and young wept in grief facing one another and did not eat for three days.
translations.idiomatic: Passing an inn, the innkeeper insulted her. Han E sang a drawn-out mournful cry, and for a li around, old and young wept in grief facing one another and did not eat for three days.

sentences.zh: 遽而追之，韓娥還，復為曼聲長歌，一里老幼，喜躍抃舞，不能自禁，忘向之悲也。

translations.literal: They hurried after her; Han E returned and again sang a drawn-out long song—for a li around, old and young leaped for joy, clapped and danced, unable to restrain themselves, forgetting their former grief.
translations.idiomatic: They hurried after her. Han E returned and sang a drawn-out long song—for a li around, old and young leaped for joy, clapped and danced, unable to restrain themselves, forgetting their former grief.

sentences.zh: 乃厚賂遣之。

translations.literal: They then gave her rich gifts and sent her on her way.
translations.idiomatic: They then gave her rich gifts and sent her on her way.

sentences.zh: 故雝門之人善歌哭，效韓娥之遺聲。

translations.literal: Therefore the people of Yong Gate are skilled at singing and weeping, imitating Han E's lingering sound.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore the people of Yong Gate are skilled at singing and weeping, imitating Han E's lingering sound.

sentences.zh: 衛人王豹處淇川，善謳，河西之民皆化之。

translations.literal: Wang Bao of Wei lived on the Qi River, skilled in song; the people west of the river all were transformed by him.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Bao of Wei lived on the Qi River and was skilled in song; the people west of the river all learned from him.

sentences.zh: 齊人綿駒居高唐，善歌，齊之右地，亦傳其業。

translations.literal: Mian Ju of Qi lived in Gaotang, skilled in song; the western lands of Qi also transmitted his art.
translations.idiomatic: Mian Ju of Qi lived in Gaotang and was skilled in song; the western lands of Qi also transmitted his art.

sentences.zh: 前漢有虞公者，善歌，能令梁上塵起。

translations.literal: In Former Han there was Duke Yu, skilled in song, who could make dust rise from the beams.
translations.idiomatic: In Former Han there was Duke Yu, skilled in song, who could make dust rise from the beams.

sentences.zh: 若斯之類，並徒歌也。

translations.literal: Such as these were all unaccompanied song.
translations.idiomatic: Such as these were all unaccompanied song.

sentences.zh: 《爾雅》曰：「徒歌曰謠。

translations.literal: The Erya says: "Unaccompanied song is called yao.
translations.idiomatic: The Erya says: "Unaccompanied song is called yao.

sentences.zh: 」凡樂章古詞，今之存者，並漢世街陌謠謳，《江南可采蓮》《烏生十五子》《白頭吟》之屬是也。

translations.literal: " As for ancient lyrics of music sections that survive today, all are street alleys' ballads and songs of Han times—Lotus Picking in Jiangnan, Fifteen Sons of the Crow, White-Haired Song, and the like.
translations.idiomatic: " The ancient lyrics of music sections that survive today are all street ballads and songs of Han times—works such as Lotus Picking in Jiangnan, Fifteen Sons of the Crow, and White-Haired Song.

sentences.zh: 吳歌雜曲，並出江東，晉、宋以來，稍有增廣。

translations.literal: Wu songs and miscellaneous pieces all came from east of the river; since Jin and Song they were slightly expanded.
translations.idiomatic: Wu songs and miscellaneous pieces all originated east of the river; since Jin and Song they have been slightly expanded.

sentences.zh: 《子夜歌》者，有女子名子夜造此聲。

translations.literal: Ziye Song—a woman named Ziye created this melody.
translations.idiomatic: The Ziye Song was created by a woman named Ziye.

sentences.zh: 晉孝武太元中，琅邪王軻之家有鬼歌《子夜》。

translations.literal: In Taixi under Emperor Xiaowu of Jin, Wang Ke's household in Langya had a ghost sing Ziye.
translations.idiomatic: During Taixi under Emperor Xiaowu of Jin, a ghost in Wang Ke's household in Langya sang the Ziye Song.

sentences.zh: 殷允為豫章時，豫章僑人庾僧度家亦有鬼歌《子夜》。

translations.literal: When Yin Yun was governor of Yuzhang, the émigré Yu Sengdu's household in Yuzhang also had a ghost sing Ziye.
translations.idiomatic: When Yin Yun governed Yuzhang, the émigré Yu Sengdu's household there also had a ghost sing the Ziye Song.

sentences.zh: 殷允為豫章，亦是太元中，則子夜是此時以前人也。

translations.literal: Yin Yun as governor of Yuzhang was also in the Taixi era—thus Ziye was a person before this time.
translations.idiomatic: Since Yin Yun's governorship of Yuzhang also fell in the Taixi era, Ziye must have lived before that time.

sentences.zh: 《鳳將雛歌》者，舊曲也。

translations.literal: Phoenix Welcomes the Fledgling Song is an old melody.
translations.idiomatic: Phoenix Welcomes the Fledgling Song is an old melody.

sentences.zh: 應琚《百一詩》云：「為作《陌上桑》，反言《鳳將雛》。

translations.literal: Ying Qu's Hundred-and-One Poems says: "Composed On the Roadside Mulberry Tree, but spoke instead of Phoenix Welcomes the Fledgling.
translations.idiomatic: Ying Qu's Hundred-and-One Poems says: "It was written as On the Roadside Mulberry Tree, but speaks instead of Phoenix Welcomes the Fledgling.

sentences.zh: 」然則《鳳將雛》其來久矣，將由譌變以至於此乎？

translations.literal: " Then Phoenix Welcomes the Fledgling has ancient origins—did it reach this state through corruption and change?
translations.idiomatic: " Phoenix Welcomes the Fledgling is of long standing—did it reach its present form through corruption and change over time?

sentences.zh: 《前溪歌》者，晉車騎將軍沈玩所制。

translations.literal: Front Stream Song was composed by Jin Cavalry General Shen Wan.
translations.idiomatic: Front Stream Song was composed by Jin Cavalry General Shen Wan.

sentences.zh: 《阿子》及《歡聞歌》者，晉穆帝升平初，歌畢輙呼「阿子！

translations.literal: Azi and Huanwen Song—at the start of Shengping under Emperor Mu of Jin, after songs ended they would call "Azi!
translations.idiomatic: Azi and Huanwen Song—at the beginning of Shengping under Emperor Mu of Jin, after songs ended people would call out, "Azi!

sentences.zh: 汝聞不？

translations.literal: Did you hear?
translations.idiomatic: Did you hear?

sentences.zh: 」語在《五行志》。

translations.literal: " The account is in the Treatise on the Five Phases.
translations.idiomatic: " The account is recorded in the Treatise on the Five Phases.

sentences.zh: 後人演其聲，以為二曲。

translations.literal: Later people developed its sound into two melodies.
translations.idiomatic: Later people developed its sound into two separate melodies.

sentences.zh: 《團扇歌》者，晉中書令王珉與㛐婢有情，愛好甚篤，㛐捶撻婢過苦，婢素善歌，而珉好捉白團扇，故制此歌。

translations.literal: Round Fan Song—Jin Director of the Secretariat Wang Min had affection with his concubine maid, love very deep; the wife beat the maid too harshly; the maid was skilled in song, and Min liked holding white round fans—thus he composed this song.
translations.idiomatic: Round Fan Song—Jin Director of the Secretariat Wang Min was deeply in love with a concubine maid. His wife beat the maid too harshly; the maid was skilled in song, and Min liked holding white round fans—so he composed this song.

sentences.zh: 《督護歌》者，彭城內史徐逵之為魯軌所殺，宋高祖使府內直督護丁旿收斂殯霾之。

translations.literal: Supervisor Song—Pengcheng Administrator Xu Kuizhi was killed by Lu Gui; Song Gaozu had palace supervisor Ding Mou collect and bury the remains.
translations.idiomatic: Supervisor Song—Pengcheng Administrator Xu Kuizhi was killed by Lu Gui. Song Gaozu had palace supervisor Ding Mou collect the body and bury it.

sentences.zh: 逵之妻，高祖長女也，呼旿至閣下，自問斂送之事，每問，輙歎息曰：「丁督護！

translations.literal: Kuizhi's wife was Gaozu's eldest daughter; she called Mou to the pavilion and asked about collection and burial; each time she sighed, "Supervisor Ding!
translations.idiomatic: Kuizhi's wife was Gaozu's eldest daughter. She summoned Mou to the pavilion and questioned him about the collection and burial. Each time she sighed, "Supervisor Ding!

sentences.zh: 」其聲哀切，後人因其聲，廣其曲焉。

translations.literal: " The tone was mournful; later people used its sound and expanded the melody.
translations.idiomatic: " Her tone was mournful. Later people took its sound and expanded it into a full melody.

sentences.zh: 《懊憹歌》者，晉隆安初，民間譌謠之曲。

translations.literal: Aonao Song—at the start of Long'an in Jin, a ballad of common corruption among the people.
translations.idiomatic: Aonao Song—a popular ballad of corrupted speech among the people at the beginning of Long'an in Jin.

sentences.zh: 語在《五行志》。

translations.literal: The account is in the Treatise on the Five Phases.
translations.idiomatic: The account is recorded in the Treatise on the Five Phases.

sentences.zh: 宋少帝更制新歌，太祖常謂之《中朝曲》。

translations.literal: Emperor Shao of Song remade new songs; the Founding Emperor often called them Central Court Melody.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Shao of Song composed new songs, which the Founding Emperor often called the Central Court Melody.

sentences.zh: 《六變》諸曲，皆因事制歌。

translations.literal: Six Changes and related melodies all compose songs according to events.
translations.idiomatic: The Six Changes and related melodies all compose songs in response to specific events.

sentences.zh: 《長史變》者，司徒左長史王廞臨敗所制。

translations.literal: Chief Clerk Transformation was composed by Wang Dan, Left Chief Clerk of the Grand Steward, facing defeat.
translations.idiomatic: Chief Clerk Transformation was composed by Wang Dan, Left Chief Clerk of the Grand Steward, as he faced defeat.

sentences.zh: 《讀曲歌》者，民間為彭城王義康所作也。

translations.literal: Reading-the-Melody Song was composed by the people for Prince of Pengcheng Yikang.
translations.idiomatic: Reading-the-Melody Song was composed by the people for Prince of Pengcheng Yikang.

sentences.zh: 其歌云「死辠劉領軍，誤殺劉第四」是也。

translations.literal: The song says "The guilty Liu the general, wrongly killed Liu the fourth"—that is it.
translations.idiomatic: The song runs, "The guilty General Liu, wrongly killed Liu the fourth"—that is the one.

sentences.zh: 凡此諸曲，始皆徒歌，既而被之弦管。

translations.literal: All these melodies at first were unaccompanied song; afterward they were set to strings and pipes.
translations.idiomatic: All these melodies began as unaccompanied song and were later set to strings and pipes.

sentences.zh: 又有因弦管金石，造歌以被之，魏世《三調歌詞》之類是也。

translations.literal: There are also cases where songs were composed to be set to strings, metal, and stone—Wei-era Three Modes lyrics are of this type.
translations.idiomatic: There are also cases where songs were composed to be set to strings, bells, and stones—Wei-era Three Modes lyrics belong to this category.

sentences.zh: 古者天子聽政，使公卿大夫獻詩，耆艾修之，而後王斟酌焉。

translations.literal: In antiquity when the Son of Heaven heard governance, he had grand officers and grand masters present poems, elders revise them, and then the king deliberates.
translations.idiomatic: In antiquity when the Son of Heaven attended to governance, grand officers and grand masters presented poems, elders revised them, and then the king deliberated over them.

sentences.zh: 秦、漢闕采詩之官，歌詠多因前代，與時事既不相應，且無以垂示後昆。

translations.literal: Qin and Han lacked the office for collecting poems; songs mostly followed former ages, neither matching current affairs nor able to be shown to posterity.
translations.idiomatic: Qin and Han lacked an office for collecting poems; songs mostly followed earlier ages, neither matching current affairs nor serving to instruct posterity.

sentences.zh: 漢武帝雖頗造新歌，然不以光揚祖考、崇述正德為先，但多詠祭祀見事及其祥瑞而已。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu of Han though he quite made new songs, did not first glorify ancestors and exalt correct virtue, but mostly praised sacrifice, visible affairs, and their auspicious signs.
translations.idiomatic: Although Emperor Wu of Han composed many new songs, he did not prioritize glorifying his ancestors and exalting correct virtue, but mostly praised sacrifices, visible portents, and their auspicious signs.

sentences.zh: 商周《雅》《頌》之體闕焉。

translations.literal: The Shang-Zhou Hymns and Eulogies form was wanting.
translations.idiomatic: The Shang and Zhou form of Hymns and Eulogies was absent.

sentences.zh: 《鞞舞》，未詳所起，然漢代已施於燕享矣。

translations.literal: Shield Dance—the origin is unclear, yet Han already used it at banquets.
translations.idiomatic: Shield Dance—its origin is unclear, yet Han already performed it at banquets.

sentences.zh: 傅毅、張衡所賦，皆其事也。

translations.literal: Fu Yi's and Zhang Heng's rhapsodies are both on this.
translations.idiomatic: The rhapsodies of Fu Yi and Zhang Heng both treat this subject.

sentences.zh: 曹植《鞞舞歌序》曰：「漢靈帝《西園故事》，有李堅者，能《鞞舞》。

translations.literal: Cao Zhi's Preface to Shield Dance Songs says: "In Han Lingdi's Western Garden story, there was Li Jian who could perform Shield Dance.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Zhi's Preface to Shield Dance Songs states: "In the Western Garden story of Han Lingdi, there was Li Jian, who could perform the Shield Dance.

sentences.zh: 遭亂，西隨段煨。

translations.literal: Caught in turmoil, he went west with Duan Gui.
translations.idiomatic: Caught in the turmoil, he went west with Duan Gui.

sentences.zh: 先帝聞其舊有技，召之。

translations.literal: The Former Emperor heard he had old skill and summoned him.
translations.idiomatic: The Former Emperor heard that he retained his old skill and summoned him.

sentences.zh: 堅既中廢，兼古曲多謬誤，異代之文，未必相襲，故依前曲改作新歌五篇，不敢充之黃門，近以成下國之陋樂焉。

translations.literal: Jian was disabled mid-career, and ancient melodies had many errors; texts of different ages need not be inherited—so following the former melody he remade five new songs, not daring to fill the Yellow Gate, merely completing base music for a petty state.
translations.idiomatic: Jian was disabled midway through his career, and the ancient melodies contained many errors. Texts of different ages need not be handed down unchanged—so following the old melody he composed five new songs, not daring to supply the Yellow Gate, but merely completing humble music for a lesser state.

sentences.zh: 」晉《鞞舞歌》亦五篇，又《鐸舞歌》一篇，《幡舞歌》一篇，《鼓舞伎》六曲，並陳於元會。

translations.literal: " Jin Shield Dance Songs also five pieces; also Bell Dance Song one piece, Banner Dance Song one piece, Drum Dance Performances six pieces—all presented at New Year's assembly.
translations.idiomatic: " Jin also had five Shield Dance Songs, plus one Bell Dance Song, one Banner Dance Song, and six Drum Dance pieces—all performed at the New Year's assembly.

sentences.zh: 今《幡舞歌》詞猶存，舞並闕。

translations.literal: Now Banner Dance Song lyrics still survive; the dances are all lacking.
translations.idiomatic: Today the Banner Dance Song lyrics still survive, but the dances are all lost.

sentences.zh: 《鞞舞》，即今之《鞞扇舞》也。

translations.literal: Shield Dance is today's Shield-Fan Dance.
translations.idiomatic: Shield Dance is the present Shield-Fan Dance.

sentences.zh: 又云晉初有《桮槃舞》《公莫舞》。

translations.literal: It also says early Jin had Cup-and-Tray Dance and Lord-Mo Dance.
translations.idiomatic: It also records that early Jin had the Cup-and-Tray Dance and the Lord-Mo Dance.

sentences.zh: 史臣按：《桮槃》，今之《齊世寧》也。

translations.literal: The historiographer notes: Cup-and-Tray is today's Qi-Era Peace.
translations.idiomatic: The historiographer notes: the Cup-and-Tray Dance is today's Qi-Era Peace.

sentences.zh: 張衡《舞賦》云：「歷七槃而縱躡。

translations.literal: Zhang Heng's Dance Rhapsody says: "Traversing seven trays while leaping lightly.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Heng's Dance Rhapsody says: "Traversing seven trays while leaping lightly.

sentences.zh: 」王粲《七釋》云：「七槃陳於廣庭。

translations.literal: " Wang Can's Seven Explorations says: "Seven trays arrayed in the broad courtyard.
translations.idiomatic: " Wang Can's Seven Explorations says: "Seven trays arrayed in the broad courtyard.

sentences.zh: 」近世文士顏延之云：「遞間關於槃扇。

translations.literal: " Recent literatus Yan Yanzhi said: "Passing in succession among trays and fans.
translations.idiomatic: " The recent literatus Yan Yanzhi wrote: "Passing in succession among trays and fans.

sentences.zh: 」鮑昭云：「七槃起長袖。

translations.literal: " Bao Zhao said: "Seven trays raise long sleeves.
translations.idiomatic: " Bao Zhao wrote: "Seven trays raise long sleeves.

sentences.zh: 」皆以七槃為舞也。

translations.literal: " All take seven trays as dance.
translations.idiomatic: " All describe the dance as performed on seven trays.

sentences.zh: 《搜神記》云：「晉太康中，天下為《晉世寧舞》，矜手以接桮柈反覆之。

translations.literal: Records of Searching for Spirits says: "In Taikang of Jin, all under heaven did Jin-Era Peace Dance, catching cups and trays with hands and flipping them.
translations.idiomatic: Records of Searching for Spirits says: "In Taikang under Jin, people everywhere performed the Jin-Era Peace Dance, catching cups and trays in their hands and flipping them.

sentences.zh: 」此則漢世唯有柈舞，而晉加之以桮，反覆之也。

translations.literal: " This means Han had only tray dance, while Jin added cups and flipping.
translations.idiomatic: " This shows that Han had only the tray dance, while Jin added cups and the flipping motion.

sentences.zh: 《公莫舞》，今之巾舞也。

translations.literal: Lord-Mo Dance is today's Kerchief Dance.
translations.idiomatic: Lord-Mo Dance is the present Kerchief Dance.

sentences.zh: 相傳云項莊劍舞，項伯以袖隔之，使不得害漢高祖。

translations.literal: Tradition says Xiang Zhuang sword-danced; Xiang Bo blocked with his sleeve so he could not harm Han Gaozu.
translations.idiomatic: Tradition holds that Xiang Zhuang performed a sword dance and Xiang Bo blocked him with his sleeve so that he could not harm Han Gaozu.

sentences.zh: 且語莊云：「公莫。

translations.literal: And said to Zhuang: "Lord, do not—
translations.idiomatic: He also said to Zhuang, "Lord, do not—

sentences.zh: 」古人相呼曰「公」，云莫害漢王也。

translations.literal: " Ancient people addressed each other as "lord"; saying "do not" meant do not harm the King of Han.
translations.idiomatic: " Ancient people addressed one another as "lord"; saying "do not" meant do not harm the King of Han.

sentences.zh: 今之用巾，盖像項伯衣袖之遺式。

translations.literal: Today's use of kerchiefs probably imitates the remnant form of Xiang Bo's sleeve.
translations.idiomatic: Today's use of kerchiefs probably imitates the remnant form of Xiang Bo's sleeve.

sentences.zh: 按《琴操》有《公莫渡河曲》，然則其聲所從來已久，俗云項伯，非也。

translations.literal: Records in Qin Melodies has Lord-Mo Crosses the River melody—then its sound comes from long ago; the folk tale of Xiang Bo is wrong.
translations.idiomatic: Qin Melodies records a Lord-Mo Crosses the River melody—its sound therefore dates from long ago. The folk tale about Xiang Bo is incorrect.

sentences.zh: 江左初，又有《拂舞》。

translations.literal: At the start of the Eastern Court, there was also Whisk Dance.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Eastern Court, there was also the Whisk Dance.

sentences.zh: 舊云《拂舞》，吳舞。

translations.literal: Formerly called Whisk Dance—a Wu dance.
translations.idiomatic: It was formerly called the Whisk Dance, a Wu dance.

sentences.zh: 檢其歌，非吳詞也，皆陳於殿庭。

translations.literal: Examining its lyrics, they are not Wu words; all are performed in the hall court.
translations.idiomatic: Examining its lyrics, they are not in Wu dialect; all are performed in the palace hall.

sentences.zh: 揚泓《拂舞序》曰：「自到江南，見《白符舞》，或言《白鳧鳩舞》，云有此來數十年。

translations.literal: Yang Hong's Preface to Whisk Dance says: "Since arriving in Jiangnan, I saw White Talisman Dance, also called White Duck-Dove Dance—said to have existed for several decades.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Hong's Preface to Whisk Dance says: "Since arriving in Jiangnan, I have seen the White Talisman Dance, also called the White Duck-Dove Dance, said to have existed for several decades.

sentences.zh: 察其詞旨，乃是吳人患孫皓虐政，思屬晉也。

translations.literal: Examining its words and intent, it is Wu people lamenting Sun Hao's tyranny and longing to belong to Jin.
translations.idiomatic: Examining its words and intent, it expresses Wu people's grievance against Sun Hao's tyranny and their wish to submit to Jin.

sentences.zh: 」又有《白紵舞》，按舞詞有巾袍之言；

translations.literal: " There is also White Zhu Dance; examining dance lyrics there is mention of kerchiefs and robes;
translations.idiomatic: " There is also the White Zhu Dance; its dance lyrics mention kerchiefs and robes;

sentences.zh: 紵本吳地所出，宜是吳舞也。

translations.literal: Zhu cloth originally came from Wu lands—it should be a Wu dance.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu cloth originally came from Wu territory—it should therefore be a Wu dance.

sentences.zh: 晉《俳歌》又云：「皎皎白緒，節節為雙。

translations.literal: Jin Banquet Song also says: "Bright bright white floss, section by section paired.
translations.idiomatic: Jin Banquet Song also says: "Bright, bright white floss, section by section paired.

sentences.zh: 」吳音呼緒為紵，疑白紵即白緒。

translations.literal: " Wu pronunciation calls floss zhu—suspected White Zhu is white floss.
translations.idiomatic: " In Wu pronunciation floss is called zhu—White Zhu is probably white floss.

sentences.zh: 《鞞舞》，故二八，桓玄將即真，太樂遣眾伎，尚書殿中郎袁明子啟增滿八佾，相承不復革。

translations.literal: Shield Dance was originally two-eight; when Huan Xuan was about to usurp the throne, Grand Music sent all performers; Palace Department Gentleman Yuan Mingzi memorialized to increase to full eight rows—handed down without further change.
translations.idiomatic: Shield Dance was originally performed in two rows of eight. When Huan Xuan was about to usurp the throne, Grand Music dispatched all performers, and Palace Department Gentleman Yuan Mingzi memorialized to increase the formation to a full eight rows—a practice handed down without further change.

sentences.zh: 宋明帝自改舞曲歌詞，並詔近臣虞龢並作。

translations.literal: Emperor Ming of Song himself revised dance melody lyrics and ordered close minister Yu He and others to compose.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Ming of Song personally revised dance lyrics and ordered his close minister Yu He and others to compose them.

sentences.zh: 又有西傖羌胡諸雜舞。

translations.literal: There were also various dances of Western Rong, Qiang, and Hu.
translations.idiomatic: There were also various dances from the Western Rong, Qiang, and Hu peoples.

sentences.zh: 隨王誕在襄陽造《襄陽樂》；

translations.literal: Prince of Sui Wang Dan at Xiangyang made Xiangyang Music;
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Sui Wang Dan composed Xiangyang Music at Xiangyang;

sentences.zh: 南平穆王為豫州造《壽陽樂》；

translations.literal: Prince of Nanping Mu at Yuzhou made Shouyang Music;
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Nanping Mu composed Shouyang Music as governor of Yuzhou;

sentences.zh: 荊州刺史沈攸之又造《西烏飛歌曲》，並列於樂官。

translations.literal: Jing Province Inspector Shen Youzhi also made Western Crows Fly song, all listed among music officials.
translations.idiomatic: Jing Province Inspector Shen Youzhi also composed Western Crows Fly, and all were listed among the music officials.

sentences.zh: 歌詞多滛哇不典正。

translations.literal: Lyrics were mostly licentious and improper.
translations.idiomatic: Their lyrics were mostly licentious and improper.

sentences.zh: 前世樂飲，酒酣，必起自舞。

translations.literal: In former ages at music feasts, when wine was heated, one always rose to dance oneself.
translations.idiomatic: In former ages at music feasts, when the wine had warmed, guests always rose to dance themselves.

sentences.zh: 《詩》云「屢舞僊僊」是也。

translations.literal: The Odes say "Repeatedly dancing lightly"—that is it.
translations.idiomatic: As the Odes say, "Repeatedly dancing lightly"—that is the reference.

sentences.zh: 宴樂必舞，但不宜屢爾。

translations.literal: Banquet music must have dance, but not repeatedly so.
translations.idiomatic: Banquet music must include dance, but not repeated dancing.

sentences.zh: 譏在屢舞，不譏舞也。

translations.literal: The criticism is at repeated dancing, not at dancing itself.
translations.idiomatic: The criticism targets repeated dancing, not dancing itself.

sentences.zh: 漢武帝樂飲，長沙定王舞又是也。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu of Han at music feasts, the Prince of Changsha Ding dancing—again this.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu of Han at music feasts and the Prince of Changsha Ding dancing are further examples.

sentences.zh: 魏、晉已來，尤重以舞相屬。

translations.literal: Since Wei and Jin, they especially valued passing the dance to the next person.
translations.idiomatic: Since Wei and Jin, people especially valued passing the dance to the next person.

sentences.zh: 所屬者代起舞，猶若飲酒以桮相屬也。

translations.literal: The one passed to rises in turn to dance, like passing cups when drinking wine.
translations.idiomatic: The person so honored would rise in turn to dance, just as cups are passed when drinking wine.

sentences.zh: 謝安舞以屬桓嗣是也。

translations.literal: Xie An danced and passed to Huan Si—this is it.
translations.idiomatic: Xie An danced and passed the turn to Huan Si—this is an example.

sentences.zh: 近世以來，此風絕矣。

translations.literal: In recent times this custom has ceased.
translations.idiomatic: In recent times this custom has died out.

sentences.zh: 孝武大明中，以《鞞》《拂》、雜舞合之鐘石，施於殿庭。

translations.literal: In Daming under Emperor Xiaowu, Shield, Whisk, and misc dances were combined with bells and stones and used in the hall court.
translations.idiomatic: During Daming under Emperor Xiaowu, Shield, Whisk, and miscellaneous dances were combined with bells and stone chimes and performed in the palace hall.

sentences.zh: 順帝昇明二年，尚書令王僧虔上表言之，並論三調歌曰：「臣聞《風》《雅》之作，由來尚矣。

translations.literal: Second year of Shengming under Emperor Shun, Ministerial Director Wang Sengqian memorialized on this and also discussed Three Modes songs: "I have heard Airs and Hymns creation has been honored since antiquity.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Shengming under Emperor Shun, Ministerial Director Wang Sengqian memorialized on the matter and also discussed Three Modes songs: "I have heard that the creation of the Airs and Hymns has been honored since antiquity.

sentences.zh: 大者繫乎興衰，其次者著於率舞。

translations.literal: In great matters they are tied to rise and fall; in lesser matters they appear in following dance.
translations.idiomatic: In great matters they are bound up with rise and fall; in lesser matters they appear in the dance of following.

sentences.zh: 在於心而木石感，鏗鏘奏而國俗移。

translations.literal: In the heart and wood and stone are moved; when struck resounding, national custom shifts.
translations.idiomatic: It resides in the heart and moves wood and stone; when resoundingly played, national custom is transformed.

sentences.zh: 故鄭相出郊，辯聲知戚；

translations.literal: Thus the Prime Minister of Zheng went to the suburbs and knew sorrow from sound;
translations.idiomatic: Thus when the prime minister of Zheng went to the suburbs, he recognized sorrow from the sound;

sentences.zh: 延陵入聘，觀樂知風。

translations.literal: Yanling entered on mission and knew custom from watching music.
translations.idiomatic: Yanling entered on a diplomatic mission and discerned the customs from observing the music.

sentences.zh: 是則音不妄啟，曲豈徒奏。

translations.literal: Then tones are not opened in vain; melodies are not played for nothing.
translations.idiomatic: Thus tones are not sounded without purpose, nor melodies played in vain.

sentences.zh: 歌倡既設，休戚已徵，清濁是均，山琴自應。
