translations.literal: Once singers are set, joy and sorrow are already signified; clear and muddy are balanced, mountain zithers respond of themselves.
translations.idiomatic: Once singers are established, joy and sorrow are already signified; when clear and muddy tones are balanced, the zithers respond of themselves.

sentences.zh: 斯乃天地之靈和，升降之明節。

translations.literal: This is the spiritual harmony of Heaven and Earth, the bright measure of ascent and descent.
translations.idiomatic: This is the spiritual harmony of Heaven and Earth, the bright measure of ascent and descent.

sentences.zh: 今帝道四達，禮樂交通，誠非寡陋所敢裁酌。

translations.literal: Now imperial way reaches in four directions, ritual and music connect—I truly dare not decide as one of narrow learning.
translations.idiomatic: Now the imperial way reaches in all directions and ritual and music are in harmony—I truly dare not judge as one of narrow learning.

sentences.zh: 伏以三古缺聞，六代潛響，舞詠與日月偕湮，精靈與風雲俱滅。

translations.literal: I submit that three antiquities lack transmitted reports, six dynasties' hidden sounds—dance and song sink with sun and moon, spirit with wind and clouds together perish.
translations.idiomatic: I submit that the three antiquities lack transmitted reports and the six dynasties' hidden sounds—dance and song have sunk away with sun and moon, and their spirit has perished with wind and clouds.

sentences.zh: 追餘操而長懷，撫遺器而太息，此則然矣。

translations.literal: Pursuing remaining melodies and long cherishing, stroking surviving instruments and deep sighing—so it is.
translations.idiomatic: To pursue remaining melodies and cherish them long, to stroke surviving instruments and sigh deeply—so it is.

sentences.zh: 夫鐘縣之器，以雅為用，凱容之制，八佾為體。

translations.literal: Bell-sets as instruments use elegance as function; Kai Rong's form takes eight rows as body.
translations.idiomatic: Suspended bell instruments serve elegant music; the Kai Rong dance takes eight rows as its standard form.

sentences.zh: 故羽籥擊拊，以相諧應，季氏獲誚，將在於此。

translations.literal: Thus feather flutes strike and clap to harmonize together—Ji's reproach will lie in this.
translations.idiomatic: Thus feather flutes strike and clap in mutual response—Ji family's reproach will lie in this.

sentences.zh: 今總章舊佾二八之流，袿服既殊，曲律亦異，推今校古，皎然可知。

translations.literal: Now Zongzhang's old row-dance two-eight stream—garments already differ, melodies also differ; comparing present to past, clearly knowable.
translations.idiomatic: Now the old Zongzhang row-dance in two rows of eight—garments already differ and melodies also differ; comparing present with past, this is plainly clear.

sentences.zh: 又歌鐘一肆，克諧女樂，以歌為稱，非雅器也。

translations.literal: Also song-bells one set harmonize women's music—named by song, not elegant instruments.
translations.idiomatic: Also, a set of song-bells harmonizes with women's music—it is named for song, not an elegant instrument.

sentences.zh: 大明中，即以宮縣合和《鞞》《拂》，節數雖會，慮乖雅體。

translations.literal: In Daming, bell-sets were combined with Shield and Whisk—phrase counts though match, I fear violating elegant form.
translations.idiomatic: In Daming, palace bell-sets were combined with Shield and Whisk dances. Though the phrase counts match, I fear this violates elegant form.

sentences.zh: 將來知音，或譏聖世。

translations.literal: Future connoisseurs may reproach the sage age.
translations.idiomatic: Future connoisseurs may reproach this sage age.

sentences.zh: 若謂鐘舞已諧，不欲廢罷，別立歌鐘，以調羽佾，止於別宴，不關朝享，四縣所奏，謹依雅則，斯則舊樂前典，不墜於地。

translations.literal: If bell-dance is already harmonized and one does not wish to abolish it, separately establish song-bells to tune feather row-dances, limited to separate banquets not affecting court sacrifice—the four bell-sets played would strictly follow elegant rule; then old music and former canon would not fall to earth.
translations.idiomatic: If the bell-and-dance combination is already harmonized and one does not wish to abolish it, then separately establish song-bells to tune the feather row-dances, limiting them to separate banquets and not to court sacrifice. The four bell-sets would then strictly follow elegant rule, and old music and former canon would not fall to the ground.

sentences.zh: 臣昔已制歌磬，猶在樂官，具以副鐘，配成一部，即義沿理，如或可安。

translations.literal: Your minister formerly already made song chime-stones, still with music officials; fitted with subsidiary bells to complete one set—following principle along reason, perhaps it can be settled.
translations.idiomatic: Your minister has already made song chime-stones, which remain with the music officials. Fitted with subsidiary bells, they form one complete set—following principle and reason, this may perhaps be acceptable.

sentences.zh: 又今之《清商》，實猶銅雀，魏氏三祖，風流可懷，京、洛相高，江左彌重。

translations.literal: Also today's Clear Shang is in essence like Copper Sparrow; Wei's three founding emperors, their elegance is cherished, the capitals held it high, the Eastern Court valued it ever more.
translations.idiomatic: Today's Clear Shang is in essence like the Copper Sparrow music of Wei's three founding emperors—their elegance is still cherished, the capitals held it in high esteem, and the Eastern Court valued it even more.

sentences.zh: 諒以金縣干戚，事絕於斯。

translations.literal: Surely because suspended metal and shield-axes—matters ended at that.
translations.idiomatic: Surely because suspended bells and shield-axes belong to a tradition that ended there.

sentences.zh: 而情變聽改，稍復零落，十數年間，亡者將半。

translations.literal: But feelings changed and listeners altered, gradually falling into decline; within a dozen years, nearly half will be lost.
translations.idiomatic: But tastes changed and audiences shifted, and the repertoire gradually declined—within a dozen years, nearly half will be lost.

sentences.zh: 自頃家競新哇，人尚謠俗，務在噍危，不顧律紀，流宕無涯，未知所極，排斥典正，崇長煩滛。

translations.idiomatic: When rivers quake and altars perish, all spirits alike are warned; grief and longing spread boundlessly, yet different ages share joy alike.

sentences.zh: 咎征不殊，而欣畏並用，竊所未譬也。

translations.idiomatic: The ominous signs are the same, yet joy and fear are invoked together—I have never understood this.

sentences.zh: 反本還源，庶可跂踵。

sentences.zh: 欲從方俗語，故名曰琵琶，取其易傳於外國也。

translations.literal: Wishing to follow local speech, thus named pipa, taking that it easily spreads to foreign lands.
translations.idiomatic: Wishing to follow local speech, it was named pipa, meaning that it could easily spread to foreign lands.

sentences.zh: 」《風俗通》云：「以手琵琶，因以為名。

translations.literal: " Customs and Manners says: "Pluck with hands—pipa—thus the name.
translations.idiomatic: " Customs and Manners says: "It is played by plucking with the hands—pipa—and thus received its name.

sentences.zh: 」杜摯云：「長城之役，弦鼗而鼓之。

translations.literal: " Du Zhi says: "At the Great Wall labor, string tambourines and drum them.
translations.idiomatic: " Du Zhi says: "During the Great Wall labor, they strung tambourines and beat them.

sentences.zh: 」並未詳孰實。

translations.literal: " None is detailed as to which is true.
translations.idiomatic: " None of these accounts clearly establishes which is true.

sentences.zh: 其器不列四廂。

translations.literal: Its instrument is not listed among the four side-chambers.
translations.idiomatic: This instrument is not listed among the four side-chambers.

sentences.zh: 空侯，初名坎侯。

translations.literal: Konghou, originally named kanhou.
translations.idiomatic: The konghou was originally called the kanhou.

sentences.zh: 漢武帝賽滅南越，祠太一后土用樂，令樂人侯暉依琴作坎侯，言其坎坎應節奏也。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu of Han after defeating Nanyue, in music for sacrifice to Grand Unity and Earth, ordered musician Hou Hui to make kanhou after the qin, saying its kan-kan responds to rhythm.
translations.idiomatic: After Emperor Wu of Han defeated Nanyue, music was used in sacrifice to Grand Unity and Earth. He ordered the musician Hou Hui to model the kanhou on the qin, saying its kan-kan sound responds to the rhythm.

sentences.zh: 侯者，因工人姓爾。

translations.literal: Hou—from the artisan's surname.
translations.idiomatic: Hou comes from the artisan's surname.

sentences.zh: 後言空，音訛也。

translations.literal: Later saying kong—sound corrupted.
translations.idiomatic: The later form kong is a corruption of the sound.

sentences.zh: 古施郊廟雅樂，近世來專用於楚聲。

translations.literal: Anciently used in suburban and temple elegant music; in recent times exclusively used for Chu sounds.
translations.idiomatic: In antiquity it was used in suburban and temple elegant music; in recent times it has been used exclusively for Chu sounds.

sentences.zh: 宋孝武帝大明中，吳興沈懷遠被徙廣州，造繞梁，其器與空侯相似。

translations.literal: In Daming under Emperor Xiaowu of Song, Shen Huaiyuan of Wuxing was exiled to Guangzhou and made Rao Liang; its instrument resembles konghou.
translations.idiomatic: During Daming under Emperor Xiaowu of Song, Shen Huaiyuan of Wuxing was exiled to Guangzhou and created the Rao Liang, an instrument resembling the konghou.

sentences.zh: 懷遠後亡，其器亦絕。

translations.literal: After Huaiyuan died, its instrument also perished.
translations.idiomatic: After Huaiyuan's death, the instrument also disappeared.

sentences.zh: 八音六曰木。

translations.literal: Sixth of the eight sounds is wood.
translations.idiomatic: The sixth of the eight sounds is wood.

sentences.zh: 木，柷也，敔也。

translations.literal: Wood: zhu, yu.
translations.idiomatic: Wood includes the zhu and the yu.

sentences.zh: 並不知誰所造。

translations.literal: Neither is known who made them.
translations.idiomatic: It is not known who made either of them.

sentences.zh: 《樂記》曰：「聖人作為椌、楬、塤、篪。

translations.literal: Record of Music says: "The sage made kuang, jie, xun, chi.
translations.idiomatic: The Record of Music says: "The sage made the kuang, jie, xun, and chi.

sentences.zh: 」所起亦遠矣。

translations.literal: " Their origin is also remote.
translations.idiomatic: " Their origin is also remote.

sentences.zh: 柷如漆筩，方二尺四寸，深尺八寸，中有椎柄，連底挏之，令左右擊。

translations.literal: Zhu is like a lacquer tube, square two chi four cun, deep one chi eight cun, with mallet handle within, connected to bottom to push—make left and right strike.
translations.idiomatic: The zhu is like a lacquer tube, two chi four cun square and one chi eight cun deep, with a mallet handle inside connected to the bottom so that left and right can strike it.

sentences.zh: 敔狀如伏虎，背上有二十七鉏鋙。

translations.literal: Yu is shaped like a crouching tiger, on its back twenty-seven studs.
translations.idiomatic: The yu is shaped like a crouching tiger, with twenty-seven studs on its back.

sentences.zh: 以竹長尺，名曰止，橫擽之，以節樂終也。

translations.literal: With bamboo one chi long, named zhi, strike horizontally— to mark music's end.
translations.idiomatic: A bamboo rod one chi long, called the zhi, is struck horizontally to mark the end of the music.

sentences.zh: 八音七曰匏。

translations.literal: Seventh of the eight sounds is gourd.
translations.idiomatic: The seventh of the eight sounds is gourd.

sentences.zh: 匏，笙也，竽也。

translations.literal: Gourd: sheng, yu.
translations.idiomatic: Gourd includes the sheng and the yu.

sentences.zh: 笙，隨所造，不知何代人。

translations.literal: Sheng—made as occasion arose, not knowing which era's person.
translations.idiomatic: The sheng was made as occasion arose—it is not known in which era.

sentences.zh: 列管匏內，施簧管端。

translations.literal: Pipes arrayed within gourd, reeds placed at pipe ends.
translations.idiomatic: Pipes are arrayed within the gourd, with reeds placed at the pipe ends.

sentences.zh: 宮管在中央，三十六簧曰竽；

translations.literal: Gong pipe at center, thirty-six reeds called yu;
translations.idiomatic: With the gong pipe at the center and thirty-six reeds, it is called a yu;

sentences.zh: 宮管在左傍，十九簧至十三簧曰笙。

translations.literal: gong pipe at left side, nineteen reeds down to thirteen reeds called sheng.
translations.idiomatic: with the gong pipe at the left side and from nineteen down to thirteen reeds, it is called a sheng.

sentences.zh: 其他皆相似也。

translations.literal: The rest are all similar.
translations.idiomatic: The rest are all similar.

sentences.zh: 竽今亡。

translations.literal: Yu is now lost.
translations.idiomatic: The yu is now lost.

sentences.zh: 大笙謂之簧，小者謂之和。

translations.literal: Large sheng is called huang, small one called he.
translations.idiomatic: A large sheng is called huang; a small one is called he.

sentences.zh: 其笙中之簧，女媧所造也。

translations.literal: The reeds within the sheng—Nüwa made them.
translations.idiomatic: The reeds within the sheng were made by Nüwa.

sentences.zh: 《詩》傳云：「吹笙則簧鼓矣。

translations.literal: Commentary on the Odes says: "Blow sheng then reeds resound.
translations.idiomatic: The commentary on the Odes says: "When the sheng is blown, the reeds resound.

sentences.zh: 」蓋笙中之簧也。

translations.literal: " This refers to the reeds within the sheng.
translations.idiomatic: " This refers to the reeds within the sheng.

sentences.zh: 《爾雅》曰：「笙十九簧者曰巢。

translations.literal: Erya says: "Sheng with nineteen reeds called chao.
translations.idiomatic: The Erya says: "A sheng with nineteen reeds is called chao.

sentences.zh: 」漢章帝時，零陵文學奚景於舜祠得笙，白玉管。

translations.literal: " In Emperor Zhang of Han's time, Xi Jing, literary scholar of Lingling, obtained a sheng at Shun's temple—white jade pipes.
translations.idiomatic: " In the time of Emperor Zhang of Han, Xi Jing, a literary scholar of Lingling, obtained a sheng at Shun's temple with white jade pipes.

sentences.zh: 後世易之以竹乎。

translations.literal: Later ages replaced them with bamboo perhaps.
translations.idiomatic: Later ages perhaps replaced them with bamboo.

translations.literal: Eighth of the eight sounds is bamboo.
translations.idiomatic: The eighth of the eight sounds is bamboo.

sentences.zh: 竹，律也，呂也，簫也，管也，篪也，籥也，笛也。

translations.literal: Bamboo: pitch-pipes, lü, xiao, guan, chi, yue, di.
translations.idiomatic: Bamboo includes pitch-pipes, lü, xiao, guan, chi, yue, and di.

sentences.zh: 律呂在《律呂志》。

translations.literal: Pitch-pipes and lü are in the Treatise on Pitch-pipes and Lü.
translations.idiomatic: Pitch-pipes and lü are treated in the Treatise on Pitch-pipes and Lü.

sentences.zh: 簫，《世本》云：「舜所造。

translations.idiomatic: As for the xiao, the Genealogical Annals says: "Shun made it.

translations.literal: " Erya says: "Bound twenty-three pipes, one chi four cun, called yan;
translations.idiomatic: " The Erya says: "Bound with twenty-three pipes, one chi four cun long, is called yan;

sentences.zh: 十六管長尺二寸者筊。

translations.idiomatic: sixteen pipes one chi two cun long is called jiao.

translations.literal: " Jiao pronounced yao.
translations.idiomatic: " Jiao is pronounced yao.

translations.literal: All xiao—also called lai.
translations.idiomatic: All xiao are also called lai.

translations.literal: Former ages had hollow xiao; the instrument is now lost.
translations.idiomatic: Former ages had the hollow xiao; that instrument is now lost.

sentences.zh: 蔡邕曰：「簫，編竹有底。

translations.literal: Cai Yong said: "Xiao—bound bamboo with bottom.
translations.idiomatic: Cai Yong said: "The xiao is bound bamboo with a bottom.

sentences.zh: 」然則邕時無洞簫矣。

translations.literal: " Thus in Yong's time there was no hollow xiao.
translations.idiomatic: " Thus in Yong's time there was no hollow xiao.

sentences.zh: 管，《爾雅》曰：「長尺，圍寸，並漆之，有底。

translations.literal: Guan—Erya says: "One chi long, one cun around, all lacquered, with bottom.
translations.idiomatic: As for the guan, the Erya says: "One chi long, one cun in circumference, all lacquered, with a bottom.

sentences.zh: 」大者曰簥。

translations.literal: " Large ones called jiao.
translations.idiomatic: " Large ones are called jiao.

sentences.zh: 簥音驕；

translations.literal: Jiao pronounced jiao;
translations.idiomatic: Jiao is pronounced jiao;

translations.literal: medium ones called nie;
translations.idiomatic: medium ones are called nie;

translations.literal: small ones called miao, miao pronounced miao.
translations.idiomatic: small ones are called miao, pronounced miao.

translations.literal: In antiquity jade was used for guan—when Shun ruled, Queen Mother of the West presented white jade guan is this.

translations.idiomatic: The Monthly Ordinances says: "Tune the qin, se, guan, and xiao.

translations.literal: " Cai Yong's commentary says: "Guan—shape one chi long, one cun around, has holes no bottom.
translations.idiomatic: " Cai Yong's commentary says: "The guan is one chi long and one cun in circumference, with holes but no bottom.

sentences.zh: 」其器今亡。

translations.literal: " The instrument is now lost.
translations.idiomatic: " That instrument is now lost.

sentences.zh: 篪，《世本》云：「暴新公所造。

translations.literal: Chi—Genealogical Annals says: "Duke Bao Xin made it.
translations.idiomatic: As for the chi, the Genealogical Annals says: "Duke Bao Xin made it.

sentences.zh: 」舊志云，一曰管。

translations.literal: " Old records say, also called guan.
translations.idiomatic: " Old records say it was also called guan.

sentences.zh: 史臣案：非也。

translations.literal: Historiographer notes: incorrect.
translations.idiomatic: The historiographer notes: this is incorrect.

translations.literal: Though not knowing which era Duke Bao Xin lived, that he was not before Shun is clear.
translations.idiomatic: Although it is not known in which era Duke Bao Xin lived, it is clear that he was not before Shun.

translations.idiomatic: In Shun's time the Queen Mother of the West presented guan—so the instrument already existed. How could Duke Xin have made the chi?

sentences.zh: 《爾雅》曰：「篪，大者尺四寸，圍三寸，曰沂。

translations.idiomatic: The Erya says: "The chi—large ones are one chi four cun long and three cun around, called yi.

sentences.zh: 」沂音銀，一名翹。

translations.literal: " Yi pronounced yin, also called qiao.
translations.idiomatic: " Yi is pronounced yin, also called qiao.

sentences.zh: 「小者尺二寸」。

translations.literal: "Small ones one chi two cun."
translations.idiomatic: "Small ones are one chi two cun."

sentences.zh: 今有胡篪，出於胡吹，非雅器也。

translations.literal: Now there is Hu chi, from Hu blowing—not an elegant instrument.
translations.idiomatic: Today there is the Hu chi, from Hu blowing—it is not an elegant instrument.

sentences.zh: 籥，不知誰所造。

translations.literal: Yue—not known who made it.
translations.idiomatic: As for the yue, it is not known who made it.

sentences.zh: 《周禮》有籥師，掌教國子秋冬吹籥。

translations.literal: Rites of Zhou has yue master, in charge of teaching sons of the state to blow yue in autumn and winter.
translations.idiomatic: The Rites of Zhou mentions a yue master, in charge of teaching the sons of the state to blow the yue in autumn and winter.

sentences.zh: 今《凱容》《宣烈》舞所執羽籥是也。

translations.literal: Today's Kai Rong and Xuan Lie dances hold feather yue—this is it.
translations.idiomatic: The feather yue held in today's Kai Rong and Xuan Lie dances are these.

sentences.zh: 葢《詩》所云「左手執籥，右手秉翟」者也。

translations.literal: This is what the Odes say "left hand holds yue, right hand grasps pheasant feathers."
translations.idiomatic: This is what the Odes mean by "the left hand holds the yue, the right hand grasps the pheasant feathers."

sentences.zh: 《爾雅》云：「籥如笛，三孔而短小。

translations.literal: Erya says: "Yue like di, three holes and short small.
translations.idiomatic: The Erya says: "The yue is like the di, with three holes and short and small."

translations.literal: " Erya says, seven holes—large called chan, medium called zhong, small called zhuo.
translations.idiomatic: " The Erya also says, with seven holes—large ones are called chan, medium ones zhong, small ones zhuo.

sentences.zh: 箹音握。

translations.literal: Zhuo pronounced wo.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuo is pronounced wo.

translations.idiomatic: As for the di, according to Ma Rong's Long Flute Rhapsody, this instrument arose in recent times and came from among the Qiang; Jing Fang completed its five tones.

sentences.zh: 又稱丘仲工其事，不言仲所造。

translations.literal: Also called Qiu Zhong skilled at it, not saying Zhong made it.
translations.idiomatic: It is also said that Qiu Zhong was skilled at it, but it does not say that Zhong invented it.

sentences.zh: 《風俗通》則曰：「丘仲造笛，武帝時人。

translations.literal: Customs and Manners then says: "Qiu Zhong made di, a person of Emperor Wu's time.
translations.idiomatic: Customs and Manners says: "Qiu Zhong made the di; he was a man of Emperor Wu's time.

sentences.zh: 」其後更有羌笛爾。

translations.literal: " Afterward there was further the Qiang di.
translations.idiomatic: " Afterward there was further the Qiang di.

sentences.zh: 三說不同，未詳孰實。

translations.literal: Three accounts differ—not detailed which is true.
translations.idiomatic: The three accounts differ, and it is not clear which is true.

translations.idiomatic: As for the jia, Du Zhi's Jia Rhapsody says: "Li Boyang made it when he entered the Western Rong.

translations.idiomatic: " An old Han commentary says: "Gu, also called the blowing whip.

translations.idiomatic: " The Jin commentary on the First Silkworm rite says: "When the imperial carriage stops, blow the small gu;

translations.literal: There is also Hu jia.
translations.idiomatic: There is also the Hu jia.

translations.literal: Han old Zheng and Di Record has its melodies, not recording origin and end.
translations.idiomatic: The old Han Zheng and Di Record contains its melodies, but does not record their origin.

translations.literal: Acclamations—probably short xiao and nao song.
translations.idiomatic: Acclamations are probably short xiao and nao songs.

translations.idiomatic: The Methods of Sima says: "When successful, then triumphant music and triumphant song.

translations.idiomatic: " The Jianchu Record also says: "Wucheng, Yellow Sparrow, Dark Clouds, and Long Journey are all mounted-blow pieces, not acclamation pieces.

sentences.zh: 」此則列於殿庭者為鼓吹，今之從行鼓吹為騎吹，二曲異也。

translations.literal: " Thus those listed in hall court are acclamations; today's traveling acclamations are mounted-blow—two kinds of pieces differ.
translations.idiomatic: " Thus those listed for the palace hall are acclamations, while today's traveling acclamations are mounted-blow—the two kinds of pieces differ.

sentences.zh: 又孫權觀魏武軍，作鼓吹而還，此又應是今之鼓吹。

translations.literal: Also Sun Quan viewed Cao Wu's army, performed acclamations and returned—this again should be today's acclamations.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Quan also viewed Cao Cao's army, performed acclamations, and returned—this too should be what are now called acclamations.

sentences.zh: 魏、晉世，又假諸將帥及牙門曲，葢鼓吹，斯則其時謂之鼓吹矣。

translations.literal: Wei and Jin ages, also granted to various generals and gate-guard pieces—probably acclamations—thus at that time called acclamations.
translations.idiomatic: In the Wei and Jin periods, acclamations were also granted to various generals and gate-guard pieces—thus at that time they were called acclamations.

sentences.zh: 魏、晉世給鼓吹甚輕，牙門督將五校，悉有鼓吹。

translations.literal: Wei and Jin ages granting acclamations was very light—gate-guard supervisors, generals, and five colonels all had acclamations.
translations.idiomatic: In the Wei and Jin periods, acclamations were granted very freely—gate-guard supervisors, generals, and the five colonels all had them.

sentences.zh: 晉江左初，臨川太守謝摛每寢，輙夢聞鼓吹。

translations.literal: Early Eastern Jin, Linchuan governor Xie Chi whenever he slept, always dreamed of hearing acclamations.
translations.idiomatic: In early Eastern Jin, Xie Chi, governor of Linchuan, always dreamed of hearing acclamations whenever he slept.

sentences.zh: 有人為其占之曰：「君不得生鼓吹，當得死鼓吹爾。

translations.literal: Someone divined for him saying: "My lord will not get living acclamations—you will get dead acclamations.
translations.idiomatic: Someone divined for him and said: "You will not receive acclamations in life—you will receive them in death.

sentences.zh: 」摛擊杜弢戰沒，追贈長水校尉，葬給鼓吹焉。

translations.literal: " Chi attacked Du Tao and died in battle, posthumously enfeoffed as Changshui colonel, burial granted acclamations.
translations.idiomatic: " Chi attacked Du Tao and died in battle. He was posthumously enfeoffed as Changshui colonel, and acclamations were granted for his burial.

sentences.zh: 謝尚為江夏太守，詣安西將軍庾翼於武昌咨事，翼與尚射，曰：「卿若破的，當以鼓吹相賞。

translations.literal: Xie Shang as Jiangxia governor went to Anxi general Yu Yi at Wuchang to consult on affairs; Yi archery-contested with Shang, saying: "If you hit the target, I shall reward you with acclamations.
translations.idiomatic: When Xie Shang was governor of Jiangxia, he went to Anxi General Yu Yi at Wuchang to consult on affairs. Yi had an archery contest with Shang and said: "If you hit the target, I shall reward you with acclamations.

sentences.zh: 」尚射破的，便以其副鼓吹給之。

translations.literal: " Shang hit the target, then with his deputy acclamations gave them to him.
translations.idiomatic: " Shang hit the target, and Yi immediately gave him his deputy acclamations.

sentences.zh: 今則甚重矣。

translations.literal: Today it is very weighty.
translations.idiomatic: Today it is highly prized.

sentences.zh: 角，書記所不載。

translations.literal: Horn—not recorded in written accounts.
translations.idiomatic: The horn is not recorded in written accounts.

sentences.zh: 或云出羌胡，以驚中國馬；

translations.literal: Some say it came from Qiang and Hu, to startle Chinese horses;
translations.idiomatic: Some say it came from the Qiang and Hu peoples, to startle Chinese horses;

sentences.zh: 或云出吳越。

translations.literal: some say it came from Wu and Yue.
translations.idiomatic: some say it came from Wu and Yue.

sentences.zh: 舊志云：「古樂有籟、缶。

translations.literal: Old records say: "Ancient music had lai, fou.
translations.idiomatic: Old records say: "Ancient music had lai and fou.

sentences.zh: 」今並無。

translations.literal: " Today both are gone.
translations.idiomatic: " Today both are gone.

sentences.zh: 史臣按：《爾雅》，籟自是簫之一名耳。

translations.literal: Historiographer notes: Erya—lai is simply one name for xiao.
translations.idiomatic: The historiographer notes: in the Erya, lai is simply another name for the xiao.

sentences.zh: 《詩》云：「坎其擊缶。

translations.literal: Odes says: "Kan—strike the fou.
translations.idiomatic: The Odes says: "Kan—strike the fou.

sentences.zh: 」毛傳曰：「盎謂之缶。」

translations.literal: " Mao commentary says: "Basin is called fou."
translations.idiomatic: " Mao's commentary says: "A basin is called fou."

sentences.zh: 築城相杵者，出自梁孝王。

translations.literal: City-building ramming-pole songs came from King Xiao of Liang.
translations.idiomatic: City-building ramming-pole songs originated with King Xiao of Liang.

sentences.zh: 孝王築睢陽城，方十二里，造倡聲，以小鼓為莭，築者下杵以和之。

translations.literal: King Xiao built Suiyang city, twelve li square, made lead-singer sounds, using small drum as beat—builders lowered poles to harmonize.
translations.idiomatic: King Xiao built Suiyang city, twelve li square, and created lead-singer chants with a small drum as beat—the builders lowered their poles in time with it.

sentences.zh: 後世謂此聲為《睢陽曲》，至今傳之。

translations.literal: Later ages call this sound Suiyang Piece—it is transmitted to today.
translations.idiomatic: Later ages called this sound the Suiyang Piece, and it is transmitted to the present day.

sentences.zh: 魏、晉之世，有孫氏善弘舊曲，宋識善擊莭倡和，陳左善清歌，列和善吹笛，郝索善彈箏，朱生善琵琶，尤發新聲。

translations.literal: Wei and Jin ages—Sun clan skilled at spreading old pieces, Song Shi skilled at beating jie and leading chorus, Chen Zuo skilled at clear song, Lie He skilled at blowing di, Hao Suo skilled at plucking zheng, Zhu Sheng skilled at pipa—especially issuing new sounds.
translations.idiomatic: In the Wei and Jin periods, the Sun clan was skilled at spreading old pieces, Song Shi at beating the jie and leading chorus, Chen Zuo at clear song, Lie He at the di, Hao Suo at the zheng, and Zhu Sheng at the pipa—they especially created new sounds.

sentences.zh: 傅玄著書曰：「人若欽所聞而忽所見，不亦惑乎！

translations.literal: Fu Xuan wrote in his book: "If people admire what they hear yet neglect what they see—is it not confusion!
translations.idiomatic: Fu Xuan wrote in his book: "If people admire what they hear yet neglect what they see, is that not confusion!

sentences.zh: 設此六人生於上世，越古今而無儷，何但夔、牙同契哉！

translations.literal: Suppose these six men were born in former ages—surpassing past and present without peer; how much more than Kui and Ya sharing accord!
translations.idiomatic: If these six men had been born in former ages, they would surpass past and present without peer—how much more than Kui and Ya sharing accord!

sentences.zh: 」案此說，則自茲以後，皆孫、朱等之遺則也。

translations.literal: " Examining this account, then from this onward all are Sun, Zhu and such men's transmitted standards.
translations.idiomatic: " According to this account, from then on all were the transmitted standards of Sun, Zhu, and the like.

sentences.zh: 宋書卷十九考證

translations.literal: Song Shu, Scroll Nineteen—Textual Verification
translations.idiomatic: Song Shu, Scroll Nineteen—Textual Verification

sentences.zh: 樂志一「以五聲和其性以八音莭其流，而故謂之樂能移風易俗平心正體焉。」

translations.literal: Treatise on Music One "use five tones to harmonize their nature use eight sounds to mark their flow, and thus call it music able to shift winds change customs level hearts correct bodies."
translations.idiomatic: Treatise on Music One: "Use the five tones to harmonize their nature and the eight sounds to mark their flow, and thus call it music, which can shift winds, change customs, level hearts, and correct bodies."

sentences.zh: 〈○尋繹文義，「故」字當在「樂」字下。〉

translations.literal: 〈○Tracing the text's meaning, the character gu should be placed below the character yue.〉
translations.idiomatic: 〈○Tracing the text's meaning, the character gu should be placed after the character yue.〉

sentences.zh: 「昔有娥氏有二女。」

translations.literal: "Formerly the E clan had two daughters."
translations.idiomatic: "Formerly the E clan had two daughters."

sentences.zh: 〈○娥一本作娀者是。〉

translations.literal: 〈○One edition has Song for E—this is correct.〉
translations.idiomatic: 〈○One edition reads Song instead of E—this is correct.〉

sentences.zh: 「乃作破斧之歌，始為東音。」

translations.literal: "Then made the Broken Axe song—first became Eastern sound."
translations.idiomatic: "Then made the Broken Axe song, which became the first Eastern sound."

sentences.zh: 〈○臣承蒼按：「既破我斧，又缺我斨」周公東征之詩也。

translations.literal: 〈○Your subject Cheng Cang notes: "Already broken our axe, also chipped our adze"—the Duke of Zhou's eastern expedition poem.
translations.idiomatic: 〈○Your subject Cheng Cang notes: "Already broken our axe, also chipped our adze"—this is the poem of the Duke of Zhou's eastern expedition.

sentences.zh: 以此為東音之始可矣，乃謂夏后孔甲田於東陽萯山取民間之子為子，其後，析橑斧斷其足，孔甲始作此歌，何其荒謬也。〉

translations.literal: To take this as the beginning of Eastern sound suffices—yet to say Xia ruler Kong Jia hunted at Dongyang Fu Mountain, took a commoner's son as his own, afterward split a beam-axe and cut off his foot, Kong Jia then made this song—how absurd!〉
translations.idiomatic: To take this as the beginning of Eastern sound suffices—yet to say that Xia ruler Kong Jia hunted at Dongyang Fu Mountain, took a commoner's son as his own, later split a beam-axe and cut off his foot, and that Kong Jia then made this song—how absurd!〉

sentences.zh: 樂器凡八音。

translations.literal: Musical instruments in all eight sounds.
translations.idiomatic: Musical instruments fall into eight sounds.

sentences.zh: 〈○諸本誤連前一行，今改正。〉

translations.literal: 〈○Various editions wrongly joined to the previous line—now corrected.〉
translations.idiomatic: 〈○Various editions wrongly joined this to the previous line—now corrected.〉
